\paragraph{Why physics behaves like the algebra of the group of order $24$.} The claim of the paper is that the forms of several different physical phenomena are recovered from this one discrete update law and a small number of assumptions, Inside by derivation and Outside at the clicks, and the reason is stated in three steps that the paper then follows. First, Outside is arithmetic in $\mathbb Q$: every measured quantity is a count at a click or a ratio of two counts (a velocity is Nodes apart over counts apart; a visibility, a correlation and a redshift are ratios of counts), and nothing measured is a real number. Second, Inside is integer and local: six operations on bounded integers at a Node and its six neighbours, each rule generic, vector and local. Written down, the rules put into every Node are the cyclic group of the phase, the group ring of the arrivals, the integer matrices of the split and the rotation, the evaluation at the roots of unity and the translation group's shift. So the state is a free $\Z$-module, and for a fixed event history the rows' block of the interval, without clicks, ends and collisions, induces an injective $\Z$-linear map on it (Theorem~\ref{th:bijection}); the whole interval is not linear, since it also holds the carry's comparison, the click's threshold and the rates read from arrivals (Section~\ref{sec:law}). Its couplings are tables: the circle's $C$ and $S$, the split's and the rotation's integer matrices, the family table. Born's rule is a coupling computed from $\Nphi$, the rungs of Eq.~\eqref{eq:rung}, so a click is a comparison of integers. Third, the transformations between click families that preserve the passage of information are the Lorentz group up to scale, the click theorem's \cite{clickframe} (Section~\ref{sec:click}), so the symmetry Outside has is the algebra's and not a metric put in. Every result the paper calls exact is an identity of that algebra under its declared tables, matrices and family table, which are inputs (the forcing ledger \cite{records}). Each is checked against the register's readings by kind; no derived prediction is tuned after its target, and where an apparatus declaration was set from the target itself (row 2a's first draft declared a lamp of $128$ periods from nature's $0.98$, withdrawn as calibrated; the run's $32$-period train is set blind \cite{closure}) the row is a calibration check and not evidence, the paper saying so; where a form was declared, the paper says so. The decisive question is how much of that the law really forces: if every phenomenon needed a rule that puts its result in beforehand, the law would explain nothing; if the same rules force several results with little freedom, that is the contribution. So the paper keeps one ledger (the forcing ledger \cite{records}): for every result, the rules of Eq.~\eqref{eq:map} it starts from, the assumptions added with their kind, the freedom left and the ground of the derivation. What can be established now is an explicit model with exact and conditional results and checks after a detector. The paper is built around the distance between that and the broad claim that Outside represents nature.

\paragraph{Where the object came from.} The object was not chosen first. One Node with six Ports, one Link per interval and bounded integers were the assumptions of a simulator; its rules, written one by one as operations on a state vector, turned out to be six maps on one ring, and the maps that preserve a Node and its causal cone turned out to be the $48$ signed permutations, their rotations the group of order $24$ (Theorem~\ref{th:group}); what did not converge to that group and that ring was not put in. The road, from the postulates to the objects they force and back, with the simulator running first and the derivations following it, is Section~\ref{sec:route}; the GameBoard the object is computed with is Section~\ref{sec:gameboard}.

\paragraph{The reading rule and the notation.} Only a detector's click is a measurement, and a click is an action of the law on the state, the one step that deletes Inside and the one row that Outside gains (the frame's assumption, P11; the law's rule \cite[section 10]{postulates}): a click, a record's moments or an external thing's reading, as the world file declares. Every physics name in this paper (Gauss's, Newton's, Coulomb's, Born's, Planck's, Tsirelson's) names the known form that the law's result recovers, Inside by derivation or Outside at a detector. A number of the GameBoard's state is
a diagnostic of the host, never compared with nature and never pinned. Every symbol is named in
English at its first use, a scalar plain, a vector in bold lowercase,
a matrix or an operator in bold uppercase; the symbol table is
in the paper's records file \cite{records}, the program's glossary is on the tree
\cite{terminology}, and every number has its one source \cite{checks}.

\paragraph{What this paper contributes, and what it does not claim.} New here: one explicitly stated update rule with its implementation, run from world files with every reading pinned before the run; exact conditional algebraic results on the lattice (the quadratic read-out characterization, the count marginals, the CHSH sum as an exact rational of the grain, $181/64$ on the registered plateau); one platform on which every formula is reached by the algebra and by the simulator alike; and a confrontation register that states the failures with the same care as the passes. Not claimed: a derivation of the Lorentz group from the six operations, the atom's levels as a reading, a unique prediction of $181/64$ without a rule that fixes the grain, or any comparison with nature beyond the rows of the full record \cite{nature,records}, each read by kind.
\section{The algebra: the group, the ring and the families}\label{sec:algebra}

This section states the object and nothing else: the words of the board, the group of the six Ports, the ring of the phase and the record as its element, the rules of one interval, the click that reads a record once, and the families as declared integers on those objects. The definitions are gathered here from the sections that used them; every later section cites them by number.

\paragraph{The definitions, in order.} Five objects, each one line of mathematics before its words, and the names used from here on.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] The GameBoard: the Nodes $\Z^3$, a box whose axes are periodic or open; the six Ports of a Node, $P = \{\pm x, \pm y, \pm z\}$, with the involution $e \mapsto -e$ (the opposite Port); one Link per interval.
\item[(2)] The group of order $24$: $G_{48} = \{g : P \to P \text{ a bijection with } g(-e) = -g(e)\}$, the $48$ signed permutations of the three axes, the symmetry group of the cube; $\det : G_{48} \to \{+1, -1\}$ a homomorphism; $G_{24} = \ker \det$, the rotations, of index $2$: the group of order $24$, the name used throughout (Theorem~\ref{th:group} states the symmetric group it is isomorphic to). The hand, a pseudoscalar, $h \mapsto \det(g)\,h$, tells the two cosets apart.
\item[(3)] The phase circle and its ring: $\Z_{\Nphi} = \Z/\Nphi\Z$, the cyclic group of the phase, $\Nphi$ declared per world; $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}] = \{\sum_p f_p x^p : f_p \in \Z\}$, its integer group ring, the addition by components and $x^p x^q = x^{p+q}$; a record's rows at one Node and label are one element $f$ of it (the paragraph ``The objects'' and Definition~\ref{def:row}).
\item[(4)] The six operations, maps on those objects: (T) $s \mapsto s + r$; (B) $(\mathbf u, \mathbf v) \mapsto \mathbf u^{\mathsf T}\mathbf C\mathbf v$ with $\mathbf C$ declared; (G) $(f, g) \mapsto f + g$ in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$; (P) a permutation of the joint state; (E) $\mathrm{ev} : \Z[\Z_{\Nphi}] \to \Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$, $\zeta_{\Nphi}$ the primitive $\Nphi$-th root of unity and $\Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$ the cyclotomic integers; (D) $s \mapsto (e, s - ed)$ with the comparison. The rules of one interval are made of them (Definition~\ref{def:rules}); each is written out below (``The six operations as maps, in symbols'').
\item[(5)] The click: $\mathrm{ev}(f)$ with its norm $|\mathrm{ev}(f)|^2$ at a detector, the one read-out (Definition~\ref{def:click}); and Outside, the counts between clicks and their ratios, the only things compared with nature (Section~\ref{sec:click}).
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{The postulates, by name.} The eleven postulates of the law keep the numbers under which Section~\ref{sec:law} states them and get a name here, used beside the number from now on: P1 bounded integers; P2 the cubic lattice, six Ports; P3 the six operations; P4 locality, a rule reads its own record and the six neighbours and nothing is kept at a Node; P5 one Link per interval; P6 one read-out, a record read once by one comparison; P7 the declared tables; P8 the families as integers; P9 the blind flight, which states the pace of a row of the beam law on its digital line, $32/55$ on a heading and $1/\sqrt3$ on the walked line, the same for every wavelength; under the detector law light is the record kind $[1, 1]$, levels at every Node, whose band $\cos\omega = \cos\omega_l(\mathbf k)$ (Eq.~\eqref{eq:dispersion}) disperses at $k^2$ by direction with no free coefficient (row A2); the two are one light in two representations \cite[1.7]{algebra}, P9 the rows' pace and Eq.~\eqref{eq:dispersion} the levels' band, and each row of the paper says which it runs under; P10 the click axiom, the click's weight the one positive quadratic form; P11 clicks only, the GameBoard read in no other way. What each forces in the algebra, and what each object gives back, are the two tables of Section~\ref{sec:route}.

\paragraph{The words of this paper.} The \emph{GameBoard} is the cubic array of Nodes, each joined to six neighbours by Links through directional Ports; time is a sequence of intervals. \emph{Inside} is the board and what moves on it, where no one measures; \emph{Outside} is the game above the board, the emitters, the detectors and their clicks, the only place a number is read. A \emph{row} is one message on the board (a Node, a direction, an age, a phase, an amount, a multiplicity and its record); a \emph{record} is the rows born together at one emitter, one quantum. The \emph{click} is a detector's one comparison, which reads a record once and deletes it: the only read-out, and the one non-local step. A \emph{rung} is one integer threshold of the click's ladder over the birth phase (Eq.~\eqref{eq:rung}); the ladder's cell the phase falls in is the outcome. Every number carries its \emph{kind}: DETECTOR, a count of clicks, the only measurement; GAMEBOARD, a number of the board's state, a diagnostic and never a result. Figure~\ref{fig:lattice} draws the board in space, Figure~\ref{fig:worlds} the two sides.

\paragraph{The six Ports, the group and the front.}
Everything geometric in the law follows from one Node and its six
Ports, $\pm x$, $\pm y$, $\pm z$, and from one Link per interval. The maps
of the six Ports onto themselves that keep opposite Ports opposite are
the signed permutations of the three axes: $3!$ orderings of the axes
times $2^3$ choices of sign, $48$ in all, the symmetry group of the cube
and of the octahedron (Theorem~\ref{th:group}). The determinant of a
signed permutation is $\pm 1$, so it splits the $48$ into two halves of
$24$: the rotations, of determinant $+1$, which are the permutations of
the cube's four body diagonals; and the improper maps, of determinant
$-1$, the reflections with the central inversion among them. The hand
of a row is that determinant made a column of the state: one
pseudoscalar bit that a map $g$ sends to $\det(g)$ times itself, so a
world with a hand reads which half a map belongs to. The same six Ports bound the pace (Proposition~\ref{prop:pace} below, the beam law's flight table, history); that the rows' pace $c$ sat at that bound and not below was the flight's declared wall $T_D$, a rule chosen among few (P9), and given the wall the value is the flight operator's norm, attained exactly on the body diagonals (the derivation's 24.1, row 9).

\begin{theorem}[the $24$ of the name]\label{th:group}
The maps of the six Ports onto themselves that send opposite Ports to
opposite Ports form the group of the signed permutations of the three
axes, of order $2^3 \cdot 3! = 48$. The determinant is a homomorphism of
this group onto $\{+1, -1\}$; its kernel, the group of order $24$ (the rotation group of the cube), has index $2$ and is the group of the permutations of the cube's four body diagonals, the symmetric group $S_4$; the other coset, the reflections, has $24$
elements too. The hand, the one pseudoscalar column of a row, which a
map $g$ sends to $\det(g)$ times itself, tells the $24$ rotations from
the $24$ reflections, as does an axial vector.
\end{theorem}

The proof is in the paper's records file \cite{records}.

\paragraph{The objects.} A record's rows at one Node and label are one
element $f = \sum_p f_p x^p$ of the group ring $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, $x$ the
generator of one phase step and $f_p$ the amount at the phase $p$; the
pointer is $\mathrm{ev}(f) = \sum_p f_p
\zeta^p$, $\zeta$ the primitive $\Nphi$-th root of unity, at the tables'
scale. The merge's cancel identifies $x^{\Nphi/2}$ with $-1$, so the rows
after the cancel are an element of $\Z[x]/(x^{\Nphi/2} + 1)$; for $\Nphi$ a
power of two (every registered $\Nphi$) that quotient is the ring of
cyclotomic integers $\Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$ itself, a free $\Z$-module of rank
$\Nphi/2$, and $\mathrm{ev}$ is the identity on it: the GameBoard's cancel and the ideal click's zero, the evaluation on $\Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$, are one relation, exactly (for an $\Nphi$ with an odd factor they are not; the register has no such $\Nphi$). The table click, Definition~\ref{def:click} with the declared integer tables, is a different map: the built click keeps the relation one way: every cancel reads $(0, 0)$, and the tables read $(0, 0)$ on more, the table pointer being a $\Z$-linear map of $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$ onto a lattice of rank $2$, its kernel of rank $\Nphi - 2$ against the cancel's $\Nphi/2$; at $\Nphi = 8192$ only $1952$ of the $8192$ table pairs are distinct and two rows of amount $1$ at the phases $0$ and $4097$ read $(0, 0)$ where $|\mathrm{ev}(f)|^2 = 4\sin^2(\pi/8192) = 5.9 \times 10^{-7}$; at $\Nphi = 64$ no zero exists with at most three rows of amounts up to $4$ (\cite{gleasonbound}, a computation from the tables, not a run), a fact of the tables and not a relation of the module. The reading is a
function $R: \Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}] \to \mathbb R$ of a cell's element, up to one
factor per record, which the multiplicity $\mathtt m$ books.

\paragraph{One group, two representations.} Under the rule of Section~\ref{sec:massive} a record at a Node is not rows with phase labels but two integers, its level now and one interval ago, $(a_{\mathrm{before}}, a_{\mathrm{now}}) = A(\cos(\varphi - k\theta), \cos\varphi)$ at the amplitude unit declared at load, $\theta = 2\pi/\Nphi$ one step and $k$ the kind's clock in whole steps per interval: two samples of the real part of one character of $\Z_{\Nphi}$ and the time translation, which fix the character, $A$ and $\varphi$, wherever the sine table's $S[k]$ is not $0$; the phase and the amplitude are both in the pair and neither is a label, and nothing else is kept at the Node (the remainder aside, on the record by verb (D)). The phase circle acts on the pair by the linear form: for every $t \in \Z_{\Nphi}$, with $\kappa = k\theta$ and $\tau = t\theta$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:linearform}
\boxed{\,\sin\kappa\,\cos(\varphi + \tau) = \cos\varphi\,\sin(\kappa + \tau) - \cos(\varphi - \kappa)\,\sin\tau\,},
\end{equation}
the angle-addition identity, proved in the algebra document \cite[1.7]{algebra}, so the record turned by $t$ is $(a_{\mathrm{now}} S[k + t] - a_{\mathrm{before}} S[t])/S[k]$ with the sine table $S[j] = \mathrm{round}(256\sin j\theta)$, an input of kind 1, the grain of the computation: verb (B) on the record's two columns and one division with the remainder kept (D), no nearest entry, no phase label, no register \cite[section 14]{declarations}; $k$ chosen so that $S[k]$ is large, the clock clause (Bell's rows $[2464, 25]$ on $\Nphi = 2048$, Malus $[308, 25]$ on $\Nphi = 256$; \cite[record 1543]{log}). The shift by $[t]$ of the group ring $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, which the beam law applies to a record's whole weight vector $f$, is here applied to the two samples of one character: the same group, the same characters, a representation of dimension $2$ in place of the regular one; the merge (G) is the rule's own addition, and the click is the rung on the pointer against the norm in place of the evaluation $\mathrm{ev}$, both one bilinear form and then one comparison (D). Three pairs, named once and never confused: a kind's pair $[\mathrm{num}, \mathrm{den}]$, the clock of a record kind, declared world data of kind 2, the table of families; a record's pair $(a_{\mathrm{before}}, a_{\mathrm{now}})$, its state; and the pair of records, one record with two arms, the Bell rows (Definition~\ref{def:click}). A reader sees one law in two representations, not two laws.

\begin{definition}[Row and record]\label{def:row}
A \emph{row} is $(x, D, \tau, p, e, h, r, \ell, w, \mathtt m)$: Node, direction,
age, phase $p \in \Z_{\Nphi}$, emitter, content per unit, record $r$, branch
label $\ell$, amount $w \ge 1$, multiplicity $\mathtt m \ge 1$. Its amplitude is
\begin{equation}
z = \frac{w}{\sqrt{\mathtt m}}\,\frac{C_{\Nphi}[p] + i S_{\Nphi}[p]}{256}, \qquad |z|^2 = \frac{w^2}{\mathtt m}\cdot\frac{C_{\Nphi}[p]^2 + S_{\Nphi}[p]^2}{65536}.
\end{equation}
Two rows equal in every field but $w$ are one row with the amounts added;
two rows of one record and label equal in every field but a phase
difference of $\Nphi/2$ are one row with the amounts subtracted (an equal pair
is no row). The state of record $r$ is an element $\psi_r$ of the free
$\Z$-module $M_r$ on the basis $(x, D, \tau, p \bmod \Nphi/2, e, h, \ell, \mathtt m)$
with $|p + \Nphi/2\rangle = -|p\rangle$; the scaling $(w, \mathtt m) \to (kw, k^2 \mathtt m)$ leaves the amplitude and the norm unchanged and is an identification at the read-out, not a relation of the module (the quotient by it would not be free, $b_1 = 2b_4 = 4b_{16} = \cdots$ for the rows $b_{\mathtt m}$ of amount $1$); the GameBoard's state is one normal form per element of $\bigoplus_r M_r$, and the multiplicity, which every split multiplies by $A$, is bounded by the law's bound of an amount, a multiplicity and a momentum component, $2^{62} - 1$ (\texttt{events/world.py}, one bit spared for one more sum), inside the host's working bound $2^{63} - 1$ for every intermediate (\texttt{core/integer.py}); a run that would pass either is refused (P1's bound, named here). In the row form of Theorem~\ref{th:isometry} a rotation multiplies $\mathtt m$ by $65536$, so four in succession would pass the law's bound; the engine does not carry that factor, keeping a record's label set and applying the tables once at the click's form, each ladder cell's weight reduced by its greatest common divisor, so the depth of successive rotations is not limited by the bound; where the bound binds, it is a limit of the implementation's domain and never a prediction. The norm is $\langle\psi,\psi\rangle =
\sum_{\text{rows}} w^2/\mathtt m$. The archived engine narrows the quotient at a
detector: rows of one record with different $\mathtt m$ at one set are added when
the ratio of the multiplicities is the square of a rational (the pointers
rescaled by the integer roots) and refused otherwise; at the tree of the
runs two multiplicities at one set were refused, and no reported world
has them, so every set below reads one $\mathtt m$.
\end{definition}

The host, not any Node, keeps per live record the birth phase $u \in \Z_{\Nphi}$,
the count of live units (amounts), an accumulated pointer $(X, Y)$ per
(Node, label) and a gathered flag. This is the apparatus's layer; the GameBoard never reads it. It is a memory no Node could own: on the two-slit
world the two paths of one record reach a pixel up to $18$ intervals
apart, so no Node ever holds both rows \cite{log}.

\begin{definition}[The update rules of one interval]\label{def:rules}
Applied in this order to every row of the beam law; item F is its flight table, the runtime before 3a9a7109, history, and under the record kind the flight is Eq.~\eqref{eq:massive}'s own.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[F] Flight: $(x, D, \tau, p) \mapsto (x + \mathrm{pos}_d(\tau+1) -
\mathrm{pos}_D(\tau),\ d,\ \tau + 1,\ p + \varphi(\tau))$, where the
family's phase turn is either an integer per Link, added only when the
step is a Link, or a pair $[n, d]$ per interval of age,
$\varphi(\tau) = \lfloor (\tau+1) n/d \rfloor - \lfloor \tau n/d \rfloor$,
counted from the row's birth or last re-emission.
\item[C] Collision: at a Node holding several rows of amount $1$ the
table permutes their directions as a function of the whole set present;
$r, \ell, \mathtt m$ unchanged; a bijection of states, not a linear map. No
collision acts in any world of this paper.
\item[S] Split, at a measured event with outputs $\{(d_i, a_i, t_i)\}$,
$a_i \in \Z$: the row $(w, \mathtt m, p)$ is absorbed and re-emitted as the rows
$(w a_i,\ \mathtt m A,\ p + t_i)$ on $d_i$ at age $0$, $A = \sum_i a_i^2$. The
balanced splitter is $(1, 1)$, $A = 2$; the reflection's turn is $\Nphi/4$.
\item[R] Rotation, at a set with setting $s$ and turn $t$, on a label
pair $(0, 1)$ read into the channels $(+, -)$:
$U_{s,t} = \begin{pmatrix} C'[s] & S'[s]\,v(t) \\ -S'[s] & C'[s]\,v(t)\end{pmatrix}$
with $v(t)$ the turn by $t$ steps on the label-$1$ column; a row of
label $0$ becomes $(wC'[s], 65536\mathtt m, p)$ on $+$ and $(wS'[s], 65536\mathtt m,
p + \Nphi/2)$ on $-$, a row of label $1$ becomes $(wS'[s], 65536\mathtt m, p + t)$ on
$+$ and $(wC'[s], 65536\mathtt m, p + t)$ on $-$ (the row form exact for $t$ a
multiple of $\Nphi/4$, the only turns used here; the archived code multiplies
the column by the tables' phasor at $t$). With $t = 0$ this is $U_s$ of
Theorem~\ref{th:isometry}; the GHZ bases below are $X = (s, 0)$ and
$Y = (s, \Nphi/4)$.
\item[M] Normal form: merge and cancel as in Definition~\ref{def:row}.
\item[B] Birth: a lamp's self-creation at interval $t$ releases record $r$
with $u$ the lamp's phase at the birth, $(b - 1) \bmod \Nphi$ for a lamp
started at $0$ that turns one step per birth, $b$ its count of births
(every world here; $b - 1 = t - 1$ only while the lamp births at every
interval; the archived code writes $(b - 1) \bmod \Nphi$ directly), rows of
amount $1$ on its $k$
directions with $\mathtt m = k$, each row's phase starting at $u$ (plus the
lamp's own turn), and, for a pair, the declared labels with integer
weights on separate arms.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\paragraph{The six operations as maps, in symbols.} Every rate and wall of Eq.~\eqref{eq:map} is made of six maps on bounded integers and nothing else. Each is written here as the map it is, the statements of the algebra document \cite{algebra} with the letters of the derivation record \cite{derivations}, on the objects above: an accumulator $s$, an integer on a line or a circle; a record's element $f \in \Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$; a vector of $\Z^3$ or $\Z^k$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(T)] \emph{The translation}, $s \mapsto s + r$ on $\Z^k$ or on a torus: every count of the law, the flight on the digital line, the phase's turn, the age, the drive, the owed count, the release, the lamp's wheel, the push per column. Where $r$ is a constant of the world the closed form is $s(t) = \lfloor s_0 + rt \rfloor$. On a row the flight's accumulator gains $2S_1N_l$ per interval ($S_1 = |D_x| + |D_y| + |D_z|$ the direction's Manhattan length, $N_l$ the label's scale, $64$ on the register) against the wall $2T_D$, started at $T_D$, so the Links crossed by the age $\tau$ are $m_D(\tau) = \lfloor (2\tau S_1N_l + T_D)/(2T_D) \rfloor$ and the $k$-th Link falls at $\tau_k = \lceil (2k - 1)T_D/(2S_1N_l) \rceil$, the flight table's closed form; on the phase a row turns $\varphi(\tau)$ steps per interval of age (Definition~\ref{def:rules}, F), read modulo $\Nphi$. The translation group of the box, $\Z_X \times \Z_Y \times \Z_Z$, is this map on Nodes.
\item[(B)] \emph{The bilinear form with a declared matrix}, $(\mathbf u, \mathbf v) \mapsto \mathbf u^{\mathsf T}\mathbf C\mathbf v$, $\mathbf C$ an integer matrix declared at load: the push, whose rate is the reader's content times the label flow $\mathbf a$ of the arriving rows through the coupling matrix, the columns with their signs (Section~\ref{sec:forces}); the split and the rotation, integer matrices on the rows (Definition~\ref{def:rules}, S and R); and the click's weight, $\mathbf f^{\mathsf T}\mathbf G\mathbf f$, $\mathbf f$ the coordinate vector of $f$ on the basis $x^p$ and $\mathbf G = \mathbf E^{\mathsf T}\mathbf E$ the tables' Gram matrix, nothing squared as a step of its own.
\item[(G)] \emph{The group-ring addition}, $(f, g) \mapsto f + g$ in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$: the merge of a record's rows at one Node, with the cancel $x^{p + \Nphi/2} = -x^p$, the passage to the quotient $\Z[x]/(x^{\Nphi/2} + 1)$, which for $\Nphi$ a power of two is $\Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$ (the paragraph ``The objects''). Two arms of a pair multiply by the ring's product, $x^p x^q = x^{p+q}$, and the labels add (Section~\ref{sec:bell}).
\item[(P)] \emph{The permutation of the joint state}: a collision permutes the directions of the single units at a Node as a function of the set present (Definition~\ref{def:rules}, C; no world of this paper runs one); a gate permutes the joint labels from the control's bit; the apportioning's tie is a rotation of an order. A permutation of directions, labels or Nodes, never of contents; a bijection of states, not a linear map.
\item[(E)] \emph{The evaluation at the roots of unity}, $\mathrm{ev} : \Z[\Z_{\Nphi}] \to \Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$, $\mathrm{ev}(f) = \sum_p f_p\,\zeta_{\Nphi}^p$: a surjective ring homomorphism whose kernel, for $\Nphi$ a power of two, is the ideal $(x^{\Nphi/2} + 1)$, the cancel of (G), so that $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]/\ker \mathrm{ev} = \Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$ exactly; and a $*$-homomorphism for the involution $f^*(x) = f(x^{-1})$, the reflection of the phase, carrying $f^*f$, the record's autocorrelation, to $|\mathrm{ev}(f)|^2$. The built evaluation is the tables at the scale $256$: the pointer $(X, Y) = \mathbf E f$, $\mathbf E$ the $2 \times \Nphi$ integer matrix of $C_{\Nphi}$ and $S_{\Nphi}$, a $\Z$-linear map into $\Z^2$ that is not a ring homomorphism ($\mathbf E(x)^2 = (64400, 12750)$ against $256\,\mathbf E(x^2) = (64256, 12800)$ at $\Nphi = 64$; COMPUTATION), whose kernel contains the cancel and more; its norm $X^2 + Y^2 = \mathbf f^{\mathsf T}\mathbf G\mathbf f$ is (B). The exact map is the algebra; the tables are the engine's declared rounding (P7).
\item[(D)] \emph{The division with the remainder kept, and the comparison}, $s \mapsto (e, s - ed)$, $e$ the event count of Eq.~\eqref{eq:map}: the count is the whole part in units of the wall, signed and truncating, the remainder in $(-d, d)$ with the accumulator's sign, the Euclidean division on a non-negative accumulator (every unsigned count); every wall crossed is the event. The comparison is part of this map: the ladder's cell of Definition~\ref{def:click}, an age against a key, a phase against a window, a threshold, each a division whose quotient is $0$ or $1$ and whose remainder is not read.
\end{enumerate}
One interval of a record applies, in this order, (T) on every accumulator, (D) whose whole part is the event, (B) at the push and at the click, (G) and (E) where rows are summed at one Node and where they end, and (P) at a collision: Eq.~\eqref{eq:map} is their composition, and nothing that is not one of the six enters it. Not one of the six, and not admitted: a root of the state at run time (the two run-time roots of the algebra document's chapter 2.7, the meeting's norm under the key \texttt{meeting} and the pushed row's pair under the key \texttt{optical}, later rules in no world of this paper; Lorentz's factor on a body's own counter), a rounded constant multiplying a row in flight beyond the tables declared at load, a float, a true division, a draw.

\begin{definition}[The click]\label{def:click}
A detector set is a subset of Nodes with a declared rung $W$, one set per Node where a screen is read per Node (an input of kind 3, the state and the apparatus). A record's wave runs on the free Nodes and passes through the set's cells; the detector's pointer accumulates its own record's motion across its cells in the units of the conserved form (Section~\ref{sec:massive}), and the click is the comparison
\begin{equation}\label{eq:click}
\boxed{\,W \times (\text{the pointer}) \ge (\text{the record's norm})\,},
\end{equation}
integers both, the crossing of the first rung $1/W$ of the norm in the detector's own count: an action of the law on the state and not a passive read, the record ending at the detector, its content entering the detector's own record, the detector's count advancing, the click stamped with that count and the record's birth stamp \cite[3.1, 8.6]{algebra}. One click per record; its completion is the click at one cell, which ends the record everywhere, its offers deleted \cite[section 10]{postulates}\cite[3.1]{algebra}, the host's one non-local step (P6); the pair's gather is that step on a record of two rows, not a second step. The weight is one bilinear form of the record's element, $\mathbf f^{\mathsf T}\mathbf G\mathbf f$ on the rows or the same form on the record's pair of levels (the paragraph ``One group, two representations''), and then one comparison; light clicks only at a detector set (a declared set of Nodes with its rung $W$); at a massive body's cells light does not click but drives the body's record through the coupling, and the body's own click reads that; a free Node has no rung, no count and no reading. For a pair, one record with two arms and two joint labels $00$ and $11$ of weight $1$ each, $\psi = (00) + (11)$ in $\Z^2 \otimes \Z^2$ tensored with its phase in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, entangled by construction, each arm's rows moving on its own line with nothing of one arm written on the other: a detector's setting is the integer $s$ of its window, and at the detector the arm's label pair is rotated by the integer matrix $\mathbf U_s$ of the half-angle tables at $1/256$, $\mathbf U_s^{\mathsf T}\mathbf U_s = n_s\mathbf I$ exactly (Theorem~\ref{th:isometry}), acting on the record's pair of levels by the linear form, one division per output, no phase read and no register \cite[section 14]{declarations}. The click of the pair is one gather at the completion over the four joint cells $(o_A, o_B)$ with the weights
\begin{equation}
R(o_A, o_B) = J(o_A, o_B)^2,\qquad J(o_A, o_B) = \sum_\ell c_\ell\,U_a[o_A][\ell]\,U_b[o_B][\ell],
\label{eq:joint}
\end{equation}
$c_\ell = (1, 1)$ in every world here; the birth wheel's $u \in \Z_{\Nphi}$, the lamp's phase at the birth, selects one cell through the rung on the cumulative weights $C_1 \le \dots \le C_K$ in the declared order,
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\,\rung_k = \left\lfloor \frac{2\Nphi C_k + C_K}{2C_K} \right\rfloor \quad (\rung_0 = 0,\ \rung_K = \Nphi),
\qquad \text{the cell is the } k \text{ with } \rung_{k-1} \le u < \rung_k\,},
\label{eq:rung}
\end{equation}
the pair's declaration \cite[3.6]{algebra}, the coarse rung over $o_A$ followed by the fine rung over $o_B$ within it with the same $u$ being how Theorem~\ref{th:marginals} states it; the settings chosen freely of the record and the reading with $c_1 = 1$ (P10) are assumed of the world; no Hilbert space is assumed. The non-locality sits in one object, the pair's record of tensor rank 2, carried by local verbs on two arms and read by one gather at two clicks.
\end{definition}


Three things are put in here and not derived, and the paper claims none
of them. Definition~\ref{def:click} recovers the Born rule's form: the weight is
the squared length of the summed pointer, and the ruler over $u$ is
inverse-transform sampling of a uniform variable, so over births with $u$
uniform on $\Z_{\Nphi}$ the count in channel $k$ is $\rung_k - \rung_{k-1}$, the
difference of two cumulative rungs, Born to the resolution $1/\Nphi$ per cell. No principle
below the square is offered. The uniformity of $u$ is an assumption about
the source: $u = (b - 1) \bmod \Nphi$ is uniform over $\Nphi$ consecutive births,
(one birth per $u$ in every run below), and its independence of the settings is a fact of a world, not of the model: $u$
is a clock and a chooser is a clock, so they are independent when the
chooser's period is coprime to $\Nphi$ and the run covers their common
period, as in this paper's choosers' world (periods $3$ and $5$ against $\Nphi = 64$). The
tables at $1/256$ are the third of these three, and a declared input of the law (Section~\ref{sec:law}, P7). What the paper derives is what
follows from these with the GameBoard's rules: the interference of one record, the exact marginals, the
$\cos^2$ correlation of the pair, GHZ's zeros, and the finite-$\Nphi$ value
of $S$. The click is the only step that removes combinations and adds a
row to the world's list; the birth is the only step that adds
combinations.

\paragraph{The families as declared integers.} Every family of the register is one row of declared integers (P8) and nothing else: the quantum $h$ ($1$ on a free family, whose rows carry their energy as turns, $0$ on a paid family, whose content is the mass), the charge per unit of content as a rational pair, the columns with their signs, the lifetime, whether the phase turns, the hand; the content $M$ of a body is the world's declaration. Written down, a family is where its quantities live: the content on $\Z$, the non-compact scale, free; the phase on $\Z_{\Nphi}$, quantised; the charge and a column's coefficient as entries of the coupling matrix; the hand a pseudoscalar under the $48$; a family's rows on the fan under the $48$; a pair's arms in $\Z^2 \otimes \Z^2$ under the settings' integer matrices; and the six verbs are the only operations on them. The mass angle $m$ of the frame is the rest pair's turn, $2\pi n/d$ per interval, a world's declaration and not the family's. The families table, in the paper's records file \cite{records}, lists every family of the register with its declared integers, its object, when it entered, the verbs that act on it and the click that reads it; a cell the tree does not name says so.      

\section{The massive record kind: the pair per kind, the band, the cone and the block}\label{sec:massive}

The law of Section~\ref{sec:algebra} was written for records that hop whole; the law as it stands today gives every record kind one declared pair of integers and lets the same six operations carry mass, a clock and a body \cite[chapter 8]{algebra}. This section states that law as the algebra document states it, before any run: each sentence carries the document's mark, proved there for every grain and every board, carried from the design's proof \cite{massiverecord}, or computed and not proved; every number is a computation declared before its run \cite{closure,declarations}, and the runs that read them are Section~\ref{sec:comparison}'s.

\paragraph{The rule with a pair per kind.} At every Node a record's row $(a_{\mathrm{now}}, a_{\mathrm{before}}, r)$ is mapped once per interval by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:massive}
3\,\mathrm{den}\;a_{\mathrm{next}} + r' = \mathrm{num}\;S_6 - 3\,\mathrm{den}\;a_{\mathrm{before}} + r, \qquad 0 \le r' < 3\,\mathrm{den},
\end{equation}
$S_6$ the sum of the six neighbours' $a_{\mathrm{now}}$ (the Node itself on a folded axis, $0$ beyond an open face), then the shift $a_{\mathrm{before}} \leftarrow a_{\mathrm{now}}$, $a_{\mathrm{now}} \leftarrow a_{\mathrm{next}}$, $r \leftarrow r'$. Light is the value $[\mathrm{num}, \mathrm{den}] = [1, 1]$; a massive kind is a value $\mathrm{den} > \mathrm{num}$, and nothing else names the mass. The verbs are (B), one entry $\mathrm{num}$ of the declared matrix on the six reads and one entry $-3\,\mathrm{den}$ on the own row's past; (T), the accumulator translated by that rate; and (D), the division by the wall $3\,\mathrm{den}$ with the remainder kept on the row, in the floor form, the remainder in $[0, 3\,\mathrm{den})$, the form whose uniqueness makes the step a bijection (the direction of time, below; \cite[8.8]{algebra}). The three tests hold: one primitive with one declared pair and no family name, light the value $\mathrm{num} = \mathrm{den}$; the three verbs on the row with no root and no float; the record's own row and its six reads, nothing kept at a Node beyond the row and its remainder.

\paragraph{The band and the pitch.} Read on a character $\cos(\omega t - \mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)$ of a periodic board, Eq.~\eqref{eq:massive} without its remainder holds exactly when $2\cos\omega = (2\,\mathrm{num}/(3\,\mathrm{den}))(\cos k_x + \cos k_y + \cos k_z)$; with light's band $\cos\omega_l(\mathbf k) = (\cos k_x + \cos k_y + \cos k_z)/3$ at the same $\mathbf k$ the same line reads
\begin{equation}\label{eq:band}
\boxed{\,\cos\omega = \cos\omega_0\,\cos\omega_l(\mathbf k), \qquad \cos\omega_0 = \mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}\,},
\end{equation}
the massive band as light's band times the pitch's cosine, proved in the algebra document for every grain and every periodic board. At $\mathbf k = 0$ the gap is the pitch $\omega_0$, the rest period $N_0 = 2\pi/\omega_0$ intervals, the rest energy $h\omega_0$, de Broglie's internal clock as the thing compared with; light has $\omega_0 = 0$, a zero mode that is a level and not a clock, so the whole difference between light and a massive record in the algebra is a gap. With $2 - 2\cos\omega = 4\sin^2(\omega/2)$ the band is light's form with the pace squared scaled by $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$, one substitution.

\paragraph{The two paces and the exact cone.} Near $\mathbf k = 0$ light's band gives $\omega_l^2 = k^2/3 + O(k^4)$, the pace $c = 1/\sqrt3$ of Section~\ref{sec:geometry} reached once more. To second order in $\omega$ and $\mathbf k$ together the massive band is Klein--Gordon's with the cone $c_m^2 = \cos\omega_0\,c^2$, a massive record's limiting pace below light's by $\omega_0^2/4$ ($0.39$ percent at $N_0 = 50$, COMPUTATION); with no truncation in $\omega_0$, at the band's bottom,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cone}
\boxed{\,\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + c_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\,k^2 + O(k^4), \qquad c_{\mathrm{eff}}^2 = \cos\omega_0\,\frac{\omega_0}{\sin\omega_0}\,c^2, \qquad \frac{c_{\mathrm{eff}}^2}{c_m^2} = \frac{\omega_0}{\sin\omega_0} = 1 + \frac{\omega_0^2}{6} + O(\omega_0^4)\,},
\end{equation}
proved in the algebra document as the expansion at the band's bottom ($1.0037$ at the pitch $\mu = 0.15$, COMPUTATION). So a bound clock in motion dilates by $\gamma_m = 1/\sqrt{1 - v^2/c_{\mathrm{eff}}^2}$ at the massive kind's own cone and not by $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$ at light's: two gammas, apart by about $\beta^2\gamma^2\omega_0^2/6$ to second order at $c_{\mathrm{eff}}$ ($0.187$ percent at $k = 3$, $\mu = 0.15$; $/4$ at $c_m$, the control), the lattice's own signature (Section~\ref{sec:comparison}).

\paragraph{Light against itself.} Light's own band, the pair $[1, 1]$, disperses by wavelength and by direction with nothing declared: along a unit direction $\mathbf n$ with $|\mathbf k| = k$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dispersion}
\boxed{\,\frac{v_g}{c} = 1 - \frac{\bigl(3\sum_i n_i^4 - 1\bigr)\,k^2}{24} + O(k^4)\,},
\end{equation}
the coefficient $0$ on a body diagonal, $1/2$ on a face diagonal, $2$ on an axis and $4/5$ averaged over the sphere (COMPUTATION, the series checked against the exact group pace \cite{lightdispersion}): a prediction of the form, the quadratic dispersion of light anisotropic on the sky with a cubic pattern and no free coefficient, its falsifier a set of bursts in different directions whose dispersion coefficients do not fit one cubic pattern once nature's sensitivity reaches the effect; nature today has bounds and no measured coefficient (row A2 of Section~\ref{sec:comparison}).

\paragraph{The block: the foreign object on the board.} A body is no new group object and no new verb: a finite set $R$ of Nodes on which the $48$ act (the block's shape; a square on a layer), declared as world data like a wall's placement; the rule of Eq.~\eqref{eq:massive} on $R$ with a lowered pair $[\mathrm{num}', \mathrm{den}']$, $\mathrm{num}'/\mathrm{den}' > \mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$, a well of the pair in the medium whose own pair is the kind's declaration, the medium's pitch $\mu$; its clock the bound mode of the map in that well, $\omega_b$, a character of the time translation at $\mathbf k = 0$, one element of $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$ carried by all the cells in step; its motion the characters of the band's surface; its momentum the existing $\mathbf p$ in $\Z^3$ and its step the existing verb (T), one integer per axis for the whole block with its remainder, the step $k$ a declaration of kind 3 and the pace of what moves the band's, below the kind's own cone; its push the stress of light's field at its outer Ports; its click the evaluation across $R$. Nothing is declared in motion: the mode's extent, frequency and regime follow from the pair and the side. The block is no element of the phase circle: its place is in the symmetry group of the cube, the shape of its cells on the board, and its action is on the phase circle, through its table, a shift $t$ of the record's phase applied in the linear form to the record's pair of levels by verb (B), one division per output, no reading of a phase and no register at a Node \cite[section 14]{declarations}; what runs on the circle is the record's phase, as for every record. Two regimes by the side $s$ against the one-Node extent: the well, $s$ small, the mode extending beyond the cells, its clock in motion Lorentz's to first order; the cavity, $s$ comparable or larger, the mode inside the cells, its clock in motion the medium's. These are the foreign objects placed on the GameBoard, the blocks, that stand for the external bodies of an experiment, and every experiment of Section~\ref{sec:comparison} is a world file of such blocks, lamps and detectors.

\paragraph{The motion, one formula and its two limits.} The moving block is a resting block of width $\gamma_m s$ along its motion with the same well, read at $1/\gamma_m$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:motion}
\frac{f}{f_0} = \frac{\omega_b(\gamma_m s, g_w)}{\gamma_m\,\omega_b(s, g_w)}, \qquad \gamma_m = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - v^2/c_{\mathrm{eff}}^2}},
\end{equation}
$f_0$ the rest clock's frequency and $f$ the moving one's, both a count between clicks on the block's own record, $\omega_b(s, g_w)$ the lowest mode of the well of side $s$ and depth $g_w$ on the world's own board, a computation per world before its run. The design derives it as the boost of the continuum operator of the band's bottom: the block's declared cells widen in its frame and never contract, and Lorentz is reached as a relation on the characters, no boost being among the $48$. On the GameBoard the formula is computed and not proved (to $0.01$ percent for $s \ge 12$ on a chain, $0.15$ percent on a layer). Its two limits are identities of the formula: in the well limit $f/f_0 \to 1/\gamma_m$, Lorentz's clock as the thing compared with; in the cavity limit $f/f_0 \to 1/\gamma_m^2$, the medium's clock; between them the first-order deviation is $\epsilon(\gamma_m^2 - 1)/2$ below $1/\gamma_m$, $\epsilon$ the mode's binding depth, the block's carried cells' mark on a bound clock and a prediction. Row 4a's number is this formula at the exact cone on its declared layer world, $0.8116$, with $0.8108$ at $c_m$ and $0.8132$ at $c$ beside it as controls (COMPUTATION \cite{closure}).

\paragraph{The coupling of the two kinds.} At a cell of $R$ the two records' rows are coupled by one entry of verb (B)'s declared matrix over the other record's two columns, the first difference both ways: the massive row gains $g\,(a_{l,\mathrm{now}} - a_{l,\mathrm{before}})$, the receive, and light's row gains $-G\,(a_{m,\mathrm{next}} - a_{m,\mathrm{now}})$, the source, both local to that cell of the block. The scheme is the Euler--Lagrange scheme of a two-point Lagrangian, so it is symplectic and has an exact quadratic invariant $J$, proved in the algebra document for every board (exact to $10^{-12}$ on a chain, COMPUTATION); the amplitude form of the coupling is withdrawn as tachyonic, its mass matrix at $\mathbf k = 0$ having a negative eigenvalue. The block emits at its mode through the same entry, a lamp at its own rest frequency, and a medium block at rest has the index $n^2 = 1 + Gg/(\omega_0^2 - \omega^2)$ in closed form, a control of the coupling with the cavity's own mode sum beside it and the $4$ percent between them open in size.

\paragraph{The detector and the click.} A detector is not an element of either group: it is a declared set of Nodes with a rung $W$, and it counts when the quadratic form of the record's values in its cells crosses $W$, the comparison $W \times (\text{the pointer}) \ge (\text{the record's norm})$, integers both, the evaluation (E) of the record on the detector's cells in the detector's own clock. A body is a detector of itself, across its own cells; a light detector is a detector set, a Node or a line of Nodes read as one Port, with a rung on the light record. Light is read by moving the record at the detector's cells, and the detector clicks; the verbs are lossless and the click needs no sink. One click per record, and the record's completion, one gather over all its detectors, is the only non-local step; nothing else leaves the Inside. Where a world must absorb it declares a take, a damping pair on light's row at the cells of an absorbing object, a declaration of the world and not the law's. What is a measurement stays the reading rule of Section~\ref{sec:click}.

\paragraph{The direction of time.} Given the neighbours' reads, the step $(a_{\mathrm{before}}, r) \mapsto (a_{\mathrm{next}}, r')$ of one row is a bijection of $\Z \times \{0, \dots, d - 1\}$ onto itself, by the uniqueness of the Euclidean division, with an exact inverse, the ceiling in place of the floor, a declared variant of the one division: the Inside is reversible to the bit for every grain and every board, and not symmetric in form, the remainder living on the later level. The click is the one deletion of the law, and the evaluation $\mathrm{ev}$ with the weight and the rung is many-to-one at every step: the arrow of time is born at the click, and at a declared take, and nowhere in the rule. The world that shows it is a check and never a pin: a train with no detector run forward and back under the exact inverse returns to its first rows bit for bit, and the same world with a detector does not, by the deleted rows exactly.

\paragraph{Known formulas and predictions.} Every row of Section~\ref{sec:comparison} carries (K), a known-formula row, the algebra's identity a textbook formula as the thing compared with and the engine reaching it the control of the engine against the algebra, or (P), a prediction row, a number the algebra gives and no known formula gives; a prediction is not a pass. The eight predictions of the massive kind, each declared before any run with its falsifier in the algebra document \cite[8.9]{algebra}: the two-pace world, a massive record's limiting pace $c_m$ below $c$ by $\omega_0^2/4$ and its bound clock at $c_{\mathrm{eff}}$; the bound clock's second term $\epsilon(\gamma_m^2 - 1)/2$; the index in motion; the hop's parametric pump; the two arms held by light alone; the atom's lines at the coupled modes' own frequencies; the click's arrow of time; and the light clock of two bodies, $N_0 = 2L/c$ plus the two ring-ups.

\section{From click to click}\label{sec:click}

Everything compared with nature is a count between clicks at a detector or a ratio of such counts; nothing inside the board is compared. This section is the chain from the ring's element read at a click to those counts and to the forms they take, the click frame under the hypotheses (A1) to (A3), each named where it enters; it uses the objects of Sections~\ref{sec:physics} and~\ref{sec:gameboard} by the names defined there. It opens with the six steps between two clicks, the two theorems of the Outside, and the one fact behind the uncertainty relation and Bell's excess; then the chain.

\paragraph{The steps between two clicks.} Every comparison in this paper walks one chain of six steps, each with its kind (DETECTOR, GAMEBOARD, COMPUTATION, CONVERSION, HOST; Section~\ref{sec:comparison}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] The birth of a record's rows at a declared source: a declaration, the family's row of integers and the world file's source with its rate against its wall; the wheel's reading $u$ is fixed here (Definition~\ref{def:rules}, B).
\item[(2)] The flight: the six operations on $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$ and the lattice, the phase turning per Link, the split and the rotation by the declared tables, the merge in the ring; the law (P3 the six operations, P4 locality, P5 one Link per interval, P9 the blind flight).
\item[(3)] The arrival at a detector and the click, the one measured event and an action of the law on the state, not a passive read (P6 one read-out, P10 the click axiom, P11 clicks only; the law's rule \cite[section 10]{postulates}): the record's wave runs on the free Nodes and passes through the detector's cells, the detector's pointer accumulates its offer, and the click is the first rung, $W$ times the pointer at or above the record's norm, in the detector's own count (Definition~\ref{def:click}); one click per record, its completion one gather over all its detectors, the law's one non-local step; the click is stamped with the detector's own count, the flight of every other record untouched, no back-action; the weight is one quadratic form of the record's element, the evaluation at the roots of unity on the rows and the same form on the pair of levels, then one comparison (DETECTOR).
\item[(4)] The detector's own count between two clicks, read under the key \texttt{clock\_stamp} (DETECTOR; a key outside this paper's law identity, Section~\ref{sec:law}, named as such where it is read).
\item[(5)] A ratio of two such counts, or a count itself (COMPUTATION on clicks; nothing of the board enters).
\item[(6)] The identity the algebra states between the ratios, the form of nature compared with.
\end{enumerate}
Step (6) is the only place where a formula meets a measurement: the click theorem gives the ratios' identity from the ring, Lorentz's factors under (A1) to (A3), Einstein's step and, in the limit under a shell average, Newton's form; a row of the full record \cite{nature,records} compares the ratio of step (5) with that identity, and with nothing else. Anything read from the board itself, a tick, a presence mean, a body's own record, a shell mean, is a GameBoard diagnostic and enters no comparison; the failures of the full record \cite{nature,records} are named by the step their earlier reading broke (Section~\ref{sec:comparison}).

\paragraph{Locality and discreteness Outside, two theorems beside P11.} Two properties of the game above the board follow and are not assumed.
\begin{theorem}[Locality Outside]\label{th:locality}
Under (A1), with the definition of Outside (P6 and P11: nothing leaves the board but clicks), every Outside event is a click and every click moves information one Node at most, so every Outside passage is a chain of clicks between neighbouring places, and the Outside inherits the Inside's locality through the conversion: no reading needs a jump, no velocity read exceeds one Node per interval of the tick, which in a detector's own count is $1/r_D$ Nodes per count, and no detector reads at a place no chain of clicks reaches. The one exception is the pair's click, one gather of one record from both settings, the law's one non-local operation.
\end{theorem}
\begin{theorem}[Discreteness Outside]\label{th:discreteness}
By the click's definition, and under (A1) with the conversion, the counts of one detector form a free abelian monoid and their ratios lie in $\mathbb Q$: every Outside quantity is an integer count or a ratio of counts. The least separation of two places read is one Link; the least time a detector times by itself is a pulse to its neighbour and its return, two of its counts at $r_D = 1$; the least step of a moving record is one Node per $k$ counts, so an elementary one-Link segment completed in $k$ counts has the velocity $1/k$, and a velocity read across $\Delta x$ Links and $\Delta n$ counts is the rational $\Delta x/\Delta n$, of resolution $1/n$ at a fixed count $n$ and dense as the counts grow; and $c$ Outside is a BOUND, at most one Link per interval on every digital line and $1/\sqrt3$ on the fan; Outside reads it as Nodes apart over counts apart with $r_D = 1$. Nothing continuous enters above the board.
\end{theorem}
Both are the click frame's, its section 0 and its closing theorem \cite{clickframe}, and Theorem 3 of Einstein Outside \cite{einsteinoutside}; neither is an added assumption. What is more than (A1) is not a theorem: that the apparatus is itself inside the law, that emitters and detectors are records of the board and not a second kind of thing, is an assumption about the world or a programme for the law; this paper marks it so and does not use it.

\paragraph{The one fact and its two faces.} One fact: a record is read once; the click reads one record into one cell of the ladder and ends it (Definition~\ref{def:click}; P6, P11). The uncertainty relation and Bell's excess are that fact seen from two sides; every claim here is the derivation's \cite[section 22]{derivations} or the click frame's \cite[section 10]{clickframe}, none new. The first face: a record is an element $f$ of $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, its position the Node its rows end at, its momentum the turn per Link (de Broglie's $\lambda = h/p$ as the declared turn, Section~\ref{sec:measurement}); the click evaluates $f$ at the $\Nphi$-th roots of unity, the discrete Fourier transform on $\Z_{\Nphi}$, so position and phase are the two sides of one transform. On the identification of the circle as position and its transform as momentum, a hypothesis of the programme and not a derivation (Section~\ref{sec:measurement}), what holds exactly and with no limit is the support bound $|\mathrm{supp}\,f|\,|\mathrm{supp}\,\hat f| \ge \Nphi$ \cite{donoho1989} (among its equality cases at $\Nphi = 64$, by enumeration: one phase and all $64$ roots, the antiphase pair and $32$, the comb of every eighth phase and $8$; COMPUTATION) and Weyl's relation $VU = \omega UV$ on $\Z_{\Nphi}$ \cite{weyl1931,schwinger1960}, which is where the law goes: $[x, p] = i\hbar$ as $\Nphi \to \infty$ with $\hbar = h_q\Nphi/2\pi = h/2\pi$, Kennard's $\Delta x\,\Delta p \ge \hbar/2$ in that limit and nothing of the law at finite grain \cite{kennard1927,robertson1929}, and at finite $\Nphi$ the entropic bound \cite{maassen1988}, the click's identity that the bits read and the bits not read of $u$ sum to $\log_2 \Nphi$ per record. What makes it an uncertainty and not a spread is the one read-out: read at a Node the record gives its position and its phase vector is erased, read on the fan's angle it gives its momentum's direction and not the Node; the two are not jointly readable because there is one click per record, and the click acts (step (3) above); the reading is what is uncertain, not the board. The second face: a lamp releases one record with two arms, the joint labels $00$ and $11$ of weight $1$, $\psi = (00) + (11)$ in $\Z^2 \otimes \Z^2$ tensored with its phase in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, its coefficient matrix of rank $2$, no $\mathbf u \otimes \mathbf v$ equal to it: entangled by construction; in flight each arm is local and nothing of one arm is written on the other; a setting is the integer rotation $U_s$ with $U_s^{\mathsf T}U_s = n_sI$ (Definition~\ref{def:rules}, R); the pair's click is one gather of the one record from both settings at its completion, the joint pointer $J(o_A, o_B) = \sum_\ell U_a[o_A][\ell]\,U_b[o_B][\ell]$, the ladder cell's weight $J^2$, the birth wheel selecting one of four cells through the ladder (Section~\ref{sec:bell}). The rows are local and the read-out is not: the non-locality sits in one object, a record of rank $2$ read by one gather at two clicks, with no signal between the arms; $E(a, b) = \cos(2\pi(a - b)/\Nphi)$ within the tables' rounding, the marginals exactly $1/2$ (Theorem~\ref{th:marginals}; no-signalling an identity of the integers), $S = 2\sqrt2$ before the rounding and $176/64 = 2.75$ at $\Nphi = 64$ (the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 1a, against $2.42 \pm 0.20$ \cite{hensen2015}), $181/64$ on the plateau (Theorem~\ref{th:bell}); Tsirelson's bound \cite{tsirelson1980} a theorem of the operator algebra on the labels; not a hidden-variable value, because the pair's weight is one quadratic form with cross terms where a mixture is linear (Fine's theorem \cite{fine1982}). What links the two faces is the same one read-out per record: it makes the support bound an uncertainty and denies Bell a hidden joint distribution. Not proven, and said so \cite[section 22.3]{derivations}: that Bell's excess is the same Fourier fact as the support bound. The standard names are the things compared with; the model's own words, the click, the record, the gather and the wheel, name the mechanism.

\paragraph{Inside and Outside, and how a click arrives at Lorentz.} This paragraph and the two after it are the conditional extension of the law, the click frame under (A1) and (A2): where (A2) enters, the result is not a consequence of the law as built, which meets (A1) only, and each line names it; the $r$-free lines follow from (A1), (A3) and the conversion alone. A packet moved Inside, from place to place, and what it says Outside: Inside, the law propagates records as a beam by the algebraic formulas of Section~\ref{sec:law}, where no one measures; Outside, the game above the board, there are detectors and their clicks only, the beam passing to them with amplitudes at the click (P11). So a thing propagates Inside as a beam, rows on digital lines at one Link per interval, and shows Outside as a wave: what a detector reads is the click's weight, the quadratic form of the record's element (Definition~\ref{def:click}, the same integer as the square of a phased sum), which adds and cancels as a phased sum at the roots of unity does, so Young's bands and the Mach-Zehnder's ports are the beam's rows read at the click and nothing else (Section~\ref{sec:measurement}); the wave is the read-out of the beam, not a second thing on the board. A detector's clock is its own record's count of what it emits and receives back, no Node holding a time and an open face without a body having none; a velocity is Nodes apart over counts apart between neighbouring detectors; the read-out is the click (Definition~\ref{def:click}). The frame \cite{clickframe}: ``To convert the lattice and the momentum inside it into motion Outside, the game above the board, one uses clicks that pass information, a click being the passage of information from Node to Node at most one Node per interval (A1) and its content an amplitude with a phase that splits each interval between staying and hopping, the mass the staying share (A2); Lorentz of the world is assumed, and what is shown is that this conversion brings it. The symmetry of the conversion, the transformations between click families that preserve (A1) and (A2), is the Lorentz group up to scale, acting on the amplitudes of the passing packet as the Dirac walk's covariance, so that the passage of clicks is Lorentz up to corrections of order $m^2 v^2$, exact in the continuum limit, a detector's own rate $\sqrt{1 - v^2}\,(1 - \kappa^2/6)$ with the mass angle $m$ the spacing over the reduced Compton wavelength; in three dimensions the lattice's anisotropy begins at the fourth order.'' (A1) and the one line, the relativity of the two directions ($k_{AB} = k_{BA}$), are special relativity's two postulates in the click language, so what is arrived at is Einstein's road walked on clicks, and what the board adds is (A2), the amplitudes that carry $\sqrt{1 - v^2}$ into a detector's own rate. The beam law's rows meet (A1), one Node per interval with the flight blind to the phase (P9), and not (A2), their hop a whole-record schedule with no staying amplitude, so their counter ran at the rest rate at every speed, $r = 1$, the rows' reading now history; under the massive record kind the clock's $1/\gamma_m$ is derived from the band's one formula (Section~\ref{sec:massive}; rows 4a, 4b) and the Lorentz group is not, the two one-way Doppler factors read through records, apart by $1 - v^2$ under the rows and by the band under the kind, the measurable that decides. No wall of the law and no declared identity enter the reading; Eq.~\eqref{eq:square} is an Inside formula on the record, read by no detector, whose Outside formulas the conversion gives. What the system gives is a computation Inside whose passage Outside is the clicks, at the quantum level as well; how far Outside represents reality is what the conversion table and the full record \cite{records} show, result by result.  \paragraph{The step beneath and the step above.} The Inside step of this chain is not Eq.~\eqref{eq:map} but the click frame's walk, one amplitude per record that splits each interval between staying and hopping (A2), whose exact invariant is $\boxed{\cos\omega = \cos m\cos\kappa}$, $\omega$ the walk's frequency per interval and $\kappa$ its momentum angle per Link; Eq.~\eqref{eq:map}, which hops whole, carries $W$ only as the declared identity of Eq.~\eqref{eq:square} (the roads table \cite{records}). The paper's centre is the step beneath, on the GameBoard, Eq.~\eqref{eq:square} in its frame, the six operations on the record with $W$ its invariant; the direction is one way: the step beneath is the axiom, the conversion of (A1) and (A2) is the map, and the step above is its image, a theorem named as what Einstein wrote. From $W$, by the conversion, the step above follows: $W c^4$ is $E^2 = E_0^2 + p^2c^2$, the gate $E_0/E'$ is $1/\gamma$, a detector's own rate, the drive's fraction is the click's velocity, and the two Doppler factors are the step above read at two detectors. The click frame's section 7 \cite{clickframe} shows the chain with no square declared: the walk's exact invariant $\cos\omega = \cos m\cos\kappa$ gives $\omega^2 = m^2 + \kappa^2 - m^2\kappa^2/3 + O(6)$; the law's own Planck map ($E = h_q n/d = h_A f$, $p = \hbar\kappa$ per Link, $E_0 = \hbar m$, the load identity $3hn = QSd$) gives $\boxed{E^2 = E_0^2 + c^2p^2}$; the whole unit $E' = E/c^2$ gives $W = E_0'^2 + 3\,\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf p$ with $3 = 1/c^2 = d$ exactly on the body diagonal ($2.954$, $2.971$, $3.000$ by direction, the root's rounding), the corrections of relative order $m^2\beta^2$, exact in the continuum limit. So $W$ is shown to that order as the conversion's identity under (A1) and (A2), no square declared anywhere in the chain \cite{clickframe2}, and Einstein's relation follows from the Inside step under (A1) and (A2), to second order, an extension the law as built does not meet, its rows hopping whole without (A2); for the rows' dynamics, which hop whole and lack (A2), $W$ remains the declared identity of \cite[record 270]{log}, the reading's identity and not yet the rows'. In one chain, with nothing of Einstein's put in: the Inside step, the click frame's walk on the record with $W$ its invariant (one amplitude per record that splits each interval between staying and hopping, (A2), whose exact invariant is $\cos\omega = \cos m\cos\kappa$; Eq.~\eqref{eq:map}, which hops whole, carries $W$ only as the declared identity of Eq.~\eqref{eq:square}); the conversion, an emitter and a click at one Node per interval (A1) and the amplitude's split (A2); the symmetry of that conversion, the Lorentz group up to scale (the click theorem); and its image, the Outside step, a detector's place apart and count apart, whose most general form above the board is Einstein's step as physics writes it, $d\mathbf p/dt = \mathbf F$ with $\mathbf p = \gamma m\mathbf v$, $E^2 = E_0^2 + c^2p^2$, $d\tau/dt = \sqrt{1 - v^2}$, and the geodesic's first terms (\cite{einsteinoutside}, section 3). Lorentz of the world is assumed, through (A1) and the relativity of the two directions ($k_{AB} = k_{BA}$), and what the chain shows is that the conversion brings it: the Lorentz group up to scale is the symmetry of the click families that preserve (A1) and (A2), and Einstein's equations are the form of the Outside step, one step above the board; nothing here derives the Lorentz group from the six verbs, and ``nothing of Einstein's put in'' says that no factor of Einstein's enters the chain's steps, not that the symmetry is derived: the step's $r$-free lines (the round trip, the composition, the aberration) are Einstein's exactly from (A1), (A3) and the conversion alone, and its scaled lines are Einstein's if and only if $r^2 = 1 - v^2$, which (A2) gives to order $m^2v^2$ and the law as built, at $r = 1$, does not. The same road serves Newton (below) and, in the same font, what it does not reach: length contraction, the perihelion's second order, the bending of light, waves, horizons and the field equations \cite{einsteinoutside}.  \paragraph{The smallest thing above.} What the Outside step is made of follows from (A1) and the click's definition with no run: a click is a Node, a detector's own count and what arrived, and the counts of a family add, so their ratios lie in $\mathbb Q$ \cite{clickframe}. Hence the least distance a click can report is one Link, Nodes apart being an integer; the least time a detector times is one count, a pulse and its return two; the least step of a velocity at $k$ counts is one Node per $k$ counts; $c$ is one Link per the least count; and the amount $w$ of a row is the unit that arrives. Every reading Outside is a whole number of these, which is why the world above the board is quantized, a theorem of (A1), (A3) and the conversion (Theorem 3 of \cite{einsteinoutside}; the velocity's quantum not read as such): physics above cannot take this from its own formulas, and the Inside gives it. The speed of light Outside is then the arrival count over the Euclidean distance, $c_D = N_l|D|/T_D$ by a row's age or by a pulse and its return, its anisotropy $1/c_D^2 = 2.954$, $2.971$, $3.000$ on the heading, the face diagonal and the body diagonal and $1/\sqrt3$ in the limit \cite{lightoutside}.  \paragraph{Newton from the small step.} The same way, with five assumptions of the law as built and no (A2) (the crowd read as the age moment, the age wall at coefficient $1$, the push, the flight blind, the reading a pulse and its return) and the spreading of $K$ beams over a shell of $N(r)$ Nodes, which is arithmetic and not a law, the fall, the equivalence principle, Kepler's ratio and the clock in a crowd come out Outside. The inverse square comes at the shell mean's rung and the equivalence exactly, $M_A$ cancelling record by record. The register's D3, T and X are their confirmation, and the inverse square's decisive reading is not made \cite{clickframe}. Every result Outside is thus the image of one Inside formula under the conversion, and The conversion table \cite{records} lists the map row by row with the reading that sits on the Outside side.  \paragraph{From an Inside formula to an Outside formula, family by family.} The same passage, written three times in full with the attributes of the row tuple of Section~\ref{sec:law} (Node, direction, age, phase, emitter, content per unit, record, label, amount, multiplicity) named at each step, so that a reader sees which attribute each formula reads and where the conversion takes it Outside. \emph{Light through two slits} (the family \texttt{light}, $h = 1$, the circle turns): the lamp puts one record on the board with two rows, one per opening, each with amount $1$, multiplicity $2$, the lamp's phase $p_0$ at birth and its own direction on the fan; Inside, each row's phase advances by the declared turn per Link along its digital line, so at the pixel $x$ the two arrive with the phases $p_1(x)$ and $p_2(x)$, the difference $\Delta(x)$ the path difference times the turn (the attributes read: direction, age, phase; the content plays no part, $h = 1$); the merge adds them, $f = x^{p_1} + x^{p_2}$ in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, and an equal pair at $\Delta = \Nphi/2$ cancels; the click evaluates $f$ at the root and squares it, $R(x) = 1024\,(65536 + C[p_1]C[p_2] + S[p_1]S[p_2])$ (the formulas of Section~\ref{sec:measurement}) (the attributes read: amount, multiplicity, phase); the rung lays the pixels on the ladder and the birth wheel selects one, the record is deleted. Outside a detector holds only its counts per pixel: over $\Nphi$ births the count at $x$ is $\rung_x - \rung_{x-1}$, proportional to $1 + \cos\Delta(x)$ within $1/\Nphi$, bright where the two ages differ by a whole turn, which is Young's law with the spacing set by the turn per Link; the reading is the bands' centres $23.5$ pixels apart for the exact law's $23.3$ (L2b, DETECTOR of the engine before 2026-09-23, history). \emph{A massive body's clock and its fall} (the families \texttt{m} and \texttt{mass}, $h = 0$, no circle): a body carries its Node, its content $M$, its momentum $\mathbf p$, an integer $3$-vector, and its counts table, each count an accumulator $(s, r, d)$; Inside, its drive moves it at the pace $|p_a|/(N_lN_wM + |p_a|)$ per axis where the axes' fires do not coincide, one Link per interval in all (the attributes read: content, momentum), its clock counts at the rate $1/(1 + a_\tau n/d)$ with $a_\tau$ the age moment of the crowd's rows at its Node (the crowd's attributes read: age, amount, direction; the body's: its counts), and the push reads the label flow $\mathbf a = \sum \mathrm{amount} \times \mathbf u_D$ of the arrivals into $\mathbf p$ (the attributes read: amount, direction, content). Recovered in the limit of the grain, with a rate: Born's rule to $1/\Nphi$ per cell and the cumulative rungs to $1/(2\Nphi)$ with the exact tables (to the tables' rounding with the declared ones, Section~\ref{sec:measurement}), Tsirelson's bound to $8/\Nphi$ plus the tables' $0.0444$ ($2\sqrt2$ in the joint limit of $\Nphi$ and $N_t$), Young's spacing, the attained value of $c$, the continuity equation's differential form. Recovered under an average that covers the shell, with the condition in the claim: Newton's inverse square, from the clicks (Section~\ref{sec:click}); Coulomb's inverse square, the retarded potential, Poisson's equation and the clock's $1/r$ form were derived from the push of the rows that hop and read on the engine before 2026-09-23, history \cite{records}. Each names the known form the algebra recovers (Gauss's, Newton's, Coulomb's, Born's, Tsirelson's, Planck's, Einstein's); the paper's own are the integer road, the finite-$\Nphi$ values (Born's bound $1/\Nphi$, the plateau $181/64$, the fixed-table limit), the quadratic read-out characterization on $\Z_{\Nphi}$ (Gleason-like), the measurable $1 - v^2$ and the entropy identity of the click (an identity of the wheel); the value $1/\sqrt3$, Tsirelson's limit and the dictionary's identities claim no novelty. Conjectured from the algebra and not read, labelled so wherever they appear (Sections~\ref{sec:delay} and~\ref{sec:discussion}, the forcing ledger \cite{records}): the bending's coefficient $2(1 + \gamma)$ on the one constant, and the atom's ladder $a_j/a_i = (j/i)^2$, $E_j \propto 1/j^2$, with Balmer's $27/20$ in the shell mean's limit; the ring's run reads its rule inside its pins and its constant outside the one-grain pin, and the ladder is computed from the algebra, not read on the board. After a detector every reading sits inside an expectation written before the run; against nature, the paper's list of Table~\ref{tab:list} is closed in the algebra before any run, every pinned reading a blank until its run is read and merged, and none is read yet on the engine as it stands; the old count of the engine before 2026-09-23 is history \cite{records}; the hypotheses beside rows 6, 13 and 14 change no verdict of the law (the full record \cite{nature,records}).
