\subsection{Geometry and symmetries: the directions and $c = 1/\sqrt3$}\label{sec:geometry}

The six Ports and their group are Theorem~\ref{th:group} of Section~\ref{sec:algebra}; the symmetries of the law and the pace follow from them.



\paragraph{The symmetries.} The law is invariant under the translations
of the box and of the interval, and under the $48$ signed permutations
of the axes, the group of the octahedron of the six Ports and of the
cube ($3! \times 2^3$; the $24$ of determinant $+1$ its rotations, the
$24$ of $-1$ its reflections, told apart by the hand, a pseudoscalar of
the group), up to the law's two declared ties, the digital line's axis order and the collision's Port order (\cite{beamlaw}, note 39 and section 4); under the circle $\Z_{\Nphi}$
exactly on the turns between events and at the click only up to the
tables' rounding; and under the permutations of the families, each with
its columns of the family table carried along \cite{familiesaudit}.
A boost, which mixes a
step in space with a step in time, is not among the $48$: Lorentz's symmetry is not a symmetry of the GameBoard but of its clicks Outside, under the amplitude split (A2) that the law as built lacks, to second order in the velocity, the GameBoard's corrections from the fourth (Section~\ref{sec:click}). The $48$
are the GameBoard's stand-in for the rotation group; angular momentum is
conserved only up to the GameBoard's grain, and no Noether theorem for the map is
claimed \cite{log}. The name of the program counts them.

\begin{figure}[!tb]\centering\includegraphics[width=0.22\textwidth]{figures/octahedron.pdf}\caption{\label{fig:octahedron}The Nodes one interval from a Node: the six neighbours are the vertices of the octahedron $|x| + |y| + |z| \le 1$, the causal front of one interval; its inscribed sphere, of radius $1/\sqrt3$, touches the eight faces on the cube diagonals and is the rows' pace $c$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:pace}); the faint cube shares the $48$ signed permutations of the axes. Drawn by \texttt{octahedron.py} from the definitions; no run.}\end{figure}

\paragraph{History: the beam law's flight table, the runtime before 3a9a7109.} This paragraph and Proposition~\ref{prop:pace} are the beam law's, its flight table, the runtime before 3a9a7109, kept as history: under the law as it stands light is the record kind $[1, 1]$ whose band disperses at $k^2$ (row A2), and $c$ Outside is a bound (Theorem~\ref{th:discreteness}). Two rules were the whole kinematics of a row: at most one Link per interval (the locality of the GameBoard) and the digital line of its direction, so that after one period of $S_1 = |D_x| + |D_y| + |D_z|$ Links its displacement is $D$ itself (straightness). The octahedron $|x| + |y| + |z| \le 1$ of the six neighbours (Figure~\ref{fig:octahedron}), scaled by the age, is the causal front, inside which every row stays; a row's mean Euclidean pace lies within $1/T_D$ of its inscribed sphere of radius $1/\sqrt3$, which touches the faces on the cube diagonals (Proposition~\ref{prop:pace}), so the vertex's pace, one Link per interval along a heading, is reached by no row's mean pace: the front is a bound and not a signal.

\begin{proposition}[The pace]\label{prop:pace}
For every primitive direction $D$, $S_1 N_l \le T_D$: the Manhattan pace
$S_1 N_l/T_D$ is at most one Link per interval on every digital line, and
$S_1 = \sqrt3\,|D|$ exactly when $|D_x| = |D_y| = |D_z|$. A pace $v$ that
is the same in every direction and at most one Link per interval on every
line satisfies $v \le |D|/S_1$ for every $D$, hence $\boxed{v \le 1/\sqrt3}$, the radius of the octahedron's inscribed sphere; and the table's Euclidean
pace obeys $1/\sqrt3 \le N_l|D|/T_D < (1/\sqrt3)(1 + 1/T_D)$ for every $D$.
\end{proposition}
The proof (Cauchy--Schwarz against $(1, 1, 1)$), the Courant and lattice Boltzmann comparisons and the ground of the bound are in the records file \cite{records}, history.

So $c = 1/\sqrt3$ Links per interval is the largest isotropic pace the two
rules allow, and the table sits at it; that it sits at the supremum and
not below is the flight's declared wall $T_D = \lfloor\sqrt{3|D|^2
N_l^2}\rfloor$, the design's third statement, a rule chosen among few
(P9; the derivation's 24.1, rows 7 and 9), not a consequence of the
two; given the wall the value is the flight operator's norm, so the
value rests on locality, straightness and the declared wall. Stated exactly: the two rules give
$c \le 1/\sqrt3$ (one Link per interval allows the pace $1$ on a heading
and only $1/\sqrt3$ on a cube diagonal, three Links for the displacement
$\sqrt3$), and what is derived is the largest uniform pace the GameBoard
allows under them; why the rows realise it, and what a detector in
motion reads of it, are not derived here (Section~\ref{sec:click}). The anisotropy is the table's rounding, below $1/T_D$ in every direction and so of order $1/(\sqrt3 N_l)$ (the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 5a, the bound on $N_l$; the bound assumes the rounding's anisotropy is of order $1/N_l$ at every $N_l$, as computed at $64$; an upper bound alone gives a sufficient $N_l$, not a necessary one); nothing measured enters the value. Stated with its ground: the pace of a direction, $N_l|D|/T_D$, isotropic within $1/T_D$, and the Manhattan bound $S_1 N_l \le T_D$ are exact in integers; the isotropic bound $1/\sqrt3$ is a theorem about a pace the same in every direction, attained on the eight diagonals, above on every other registered direction, and a limit of the grain $N_l$.





\subsection{Conservation, the flux and the forces}\label{sec:forces}

\paragraph{The books.} Every message released is on exactly one line of
the books at every interval, released equals in transit plus absorbed
plus escaped plus cancelled, per family, in amount and in content,
exact at every interval and at every operation (P3, P5): the carry is a
bijection $s \mapsto (e, s - ed)$ that loses nothing, and the split and
the rotation are integer matrices whose conjugate transposes invert them
(Theorem~\ref{th:isometry}). From the books the continuity equation of
the content follows exactly on the GameBoard (the derivation's 25.4
\cite{derivations}); it is the first row of the ledger. A paid message
carries its label out of its emitter at birth and into its reader at
its end, so for paid messages momentum is conserved and the third law
holds message by message; a free message, a field's row, takes no
recoil at birth and pushes its reader by its label times the reader's
content. For a free family the third law is a symmetry of two readers, body A pushed by B's field and B by A's, the two pushes $-M_A\mathbf a_B$ and $-M_B\mathbf a_A$ ($M$ the content, $\mathbf a$ the acceleration the other's field gives) equal and opposite, and not a balance per message; the momentum lines of the free books are a report of the GameBoard, and the momentum of the bodies and the field together is not booked as conserved (the derivation's 9.1 and 12.4 \cite{derivations}).

\paragraph{Gauss's law, exact.} The walk is a translation: a free unit
released inside a closed surface that no periodic axis crosses, with no
absorbing reader inside it and within the unit's lifetime, crosses the surface outward once more than inward (a non-convex surface it may leave, re-enter and leave again, the signed crossings summing to one, the crossing counted with the sign of the Port's outward normal; no splitter, absorber or cancelling pair inside the surface; no collision acts on a fan or on lone beams), so once the front has passed, the net amount crossing the surface per interval equals the release inside it for a constant release, exactly, and for a varying release the crossings at the interval $t$ equal the releases at the retarded intervals, direction by direction. The crossings of an interior surface are the host's count (GAMEBOARD, a diagnostic); a face's border clicks are a detector's (DETECTOR). Proved from the
definitions under those conditions; no detector reading of it is
registered.

\subsection{Measurement and the quadratic form}\label{sec:measurement}

The worlds of this section have no body: the law of Section~\ref{sec:law}
on rows alone, and the measurement is the one threshold that is read
out. Every interval applies three of the six operations to the state,
the translation (the flight, the phase, every count and the birth), the
multiplication by a declared integer matrix (the split and the
rotation) and the sum in the group ring (the merge, where opposite
phases cancel); between clicks the rates are constant, so the map has a
closed form and every count of Section~\ref{sec:checks} was computed
from it before its run. The click is the one place with a fourth
operation: the apparatus sums a record's rows through the tables and
squares the sum, the norm, and only then applies its threshold to the
birth phase $u$.

The row and the record, the update rules of one interval and the click are Definitions~\ref{def:row}, \ref{def:rules} and~\ref{def:click} of Section~\ref{sec:algebra}, one click per record by that Definition.

\paragraph{The two theorems of the interval.} Two theorems of the
linear block are stated here and proved in the paper's records file \cite{records}.

\begin{theorem}[The split is an isometry whose conjugate transpose inverts it]\label{th:isometry}
The split $(w, \mathtt m, p) \mapsto ((wa_i, \mathtt m A, p + t_i))_i$ preserves
$\sum w^2/\mathtt m$ for every nonzero integer vector $(a_i)$, and the conjugate
transpose of the table (the same weights with the turns reversed)
applied to its outputs, followed by the normal form, returns the input up
to the scaling $(kw, k^2\mathtt m)$ with $k = A$. The rotation satisfies
$U_s^{\mathsf T} U_s = n_s I$ exactly with $n_s = C'[s]^2 + S'[s]^2$, and
multiplies a record's norm by $n_s/65536$: an isometry only up to the
tables' rounding ($65705/65536$ at $\Nphi = 64$, $s = 1$).
\end{theorem}
\begin{theorem}[The interval is injective between clicks]\label{th:bijection}
Let $Q$ be the quotient of $\bigoplus_r M_r$ that forgets the age (rows differing only in their age identified), and fix the event history of the record, the intervals and Nodes of its births, splits, rotations and re-emissions, which the record keeps. For an interval without a click, an end at a face or the border, or a collision, and for splitters whose joint table $B$ (one column per input, the entries $a_i x^{t_i}$ in the group ring) satisfies $B^{\mathsf H} B = A I$, the balanced splitter with the turn $\Nphi/4$ among them, $M \circ R \circ S \circ F$ induces an injective $\Z$-linear map of $Q$ into itself: no rule of the interval deletes a weight, a multiplicity or a phase, and the state at any interval between two clicks, with the history, determines them at the birth. The age is not a coordinate of $Q$ but a function of the history, the current interval less the interval of the row's last event; a split restarts it at $0$ by the definition of age (Definition~\ref{def:rules}) and forgets nothing, since the interval of the split is in the history; the click is the one deletion. A
collision, where it acts, is a bijection of the GameBoard's states that
is not linear; none acts in the worlds of this paper. The theorem is of the rows' linear block; a body's drive, whose later coincident fire is lost under the engine's rule (P5, Section~\ref{sec:law}), is outside it and is not injective in that case.
\end{theorem}
So a record's norm is conserved exactly by $S$ and by the flight, and by
$R$ and by every read through the tables only within the tables' rounding
(Appendix~\ref{app:technical}). The normalisation by $C_K$ in \eqref{eq:rung} makes
the click's probabilities sum to one at completion; it does not restore
the norm along the way, and the paper claims exact unitarity nowhere.

\paragraph{The click's square as a positive quadratic form: a quadratic read-out characterization.}

The row of the forcing ledger \cite{records} on the click's weight is written out here from the derivation's section 6.5 \cite{derivations}; the register's checks are series L's clicks (Section~\ref{sec:checks}). The click's square, the norm of a record's summed pointer, is the one
operation of the law beyond the translation, the wall, the declared
matrix and the addition, and the place where the Born rule enters.
Asked: whether the operations of Section~\ref{sec:law}, with one hypothesis on the
reading, force the reading at a click to be that square, or what weaker
statement holds and what the register pins.

The objects are those of Section~\ref{sec:algebra}: the record's element $f$ of $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, its pointer $\mathrm{ev}(f)$ and the function $R$ of a cell's element.

\paragraph{The hypotheses.} (a) The phase rotation, $R(xf) = R(f)$: a
rotation of the record's phase by one step changes no weight (the rungs
take no $u$; $u$ only selects among them), an operation of Section~\ref{sec:law}. (b)
The balanced splitter conserves the reading for every two inputs,
$R(x^{\Nphi/4} f + g) + R(f + x^{\Nphi/4} g) = A_2\,(R(f) + R(g))$ for all $f,
g$ (the $(1, 1)$ split with the quarter turn on the reflected row, $A_2$
its multiplicity factor): a hypothesis on the reading, stronger than
Section~\ref{sec:law}'s split, which is an integer matrix on rows and says nothing of
what a detector reads under it; the register checks it only on the
registered pairs (the totals $64/0$ and $32/32$ of Section~\ref{sec:checks}). (c)
Counts, $R(f) \ge 0$. (d) The empty reads zero: $R(0) = 0$ on the zero
count vector. (e) Some input reads: $R$ is not identically zero.
Without (d) the hypotheses admit a detector that always reads $1$,
which satisfies (a), (b) with $A_2 = 1$ and (c) and is no quadratic
form; without (e) they admit the zero detector, under which (b) holds
for every $A_2$; so (a) to (c) alone do not force the square. (d) and
(e) are what the engine does (the Gram form on the empty record is
$0$; a click needs a live unit) and what the proof's first step uses
(\cite[record 340]{log}; the derivation's 6.5 restated with them). Not assumed: continuity, a dimension, the form of $R$ on
one row, or Theorem~\ref{th:isometry}'s $A = \sum a_i^2$.

\begin{theorem}[The quadratic read-out on the phase lattice, a Gleason-like characterization]\label{th:gleason}
Under (a) to (e), with $\Nphi$ a power of two, $A_2 = 2$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gleason}
\boxed{\,R(f) = \sum_{j\ \mathrm{odd},\ 1 \le j < \Nphi/2} c_j\,|\sigma_j(f)|^2, \qquad c_j \ge 0,
\qquad \sigma_j(f) = \sum_p f_p\,e^{2\pi i j p/\Nphi}\,},
\end{equation}
the $\sigma_j$ the Galois conjugates of $\mathrm{ev}$, $\sigma_1 =
\mathrm{ev}$. Every such $R$ is a positive quadratic form on the lattice,
homogeneous, $R(af) = a^2 R(f)$; it conserves the total at every
declared split of one row or of two recombining inputs exactly if and
only if the multiplicity factor is $A = \sum a_i^2$, and at every label
rotation with the factor $C'^2 + S'^2$, $C'$ and $S'$ the half-angle
tables of Definition~\ref{def:rules}. Two rows $ax^p$ and $bx^{p+\Delta}$ at one Node,
$\Delta$ their phase difference in steps, read $R = C_\Sigma(a^2 + b^2)
+ 2ab\,\mathcal K(\Delta)$ with $C_\Sigma = \sum c_j$ and
$\mathcal K(\Delta) = \sum c_j \cos(2\pi j\Delta/\Nphi)$, $\mathcal K(0) =
C_\Sigma$, $\mathcal K(\Nphi/4) = 0$, $\mathcal K(\Nphi/2) = -C_\Sigma$ for every
admissible $R$; the Born form $|\mathrm{ev}(f)|^2$ is $c_1 = 1$ and the
other $c_j = 0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Sketch; the derivation's 6.5 \cite{derivations} gives the steps in
full under (a) to (e). (i) $g = 0$ in (b) with (a) gives $2R(f) =
A_2\,(R(f) + R(0)) = A_2 R(f)$ by (d), so $A_2 = 2$, one $f$ with $R(f)
> 0$ sufficing, and (e) supplies it. (ii) Replacing $g$ by $x^{-\Nphi/4}g$ in (b) and
using (a) and $x^{-\Nphi/2} = -1$ gives $R(f - g) + R(f + g) = 2R(f) +
2R(g)$, the parallelogram law on the abelian group $\Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$. (iii)
The parallelogram law alone makes $R$ a quadratic form: on a lattice the
argument of Jordan and von Neumann \cite{jordan1935} needs no
continuity, and $R(f) = B(f, f)/2$ with $B$ a $\Z$-bilinear symmetric
form, the restriction of the real form of a symmetric matrix $\mathbf
G$, the click's Gram matrix (not the fan's grain $N_\theta$ of Section~\ref{sec:law}). (iv) By (a), $\mathbf G$ commutes with the signed permutation of
the basis that multiplication by $x$ is, whose eigen-functionals are the
$\sigma_j$, $j$ odd; so $\mathbf G$ is diagonal in that basis with real
entries paired under $j \leftrightarrow -j$. (v) A negative $c_j$ would
make the form negative on an open cone containing lattice points,
against (c). (vi) The conservation at a general split and at a label
rotation follows from homogeneity, (a) and the cancellation of the
cross terms between the two outputs; for two inputs recombining at one split it needs $\mathbf B^{\mathsf H}\mathbf B = A\,\mathbf I$ per character, which the balanced table meets, the declared splitter being that case. (vii) Two rows: $|\sigma_j(a +
bx^\Delta)|^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab\cos(2\pi j\Delta/\Nphi)$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{What is derived and what is not.} Derived from the update rules and the axiom (b): the reading is a positive quadratic form of the record's element, forced by the rotation, the balanced splitter's conservation and the counts alone, with no continuity and no dimension (Gleason's theorem \cite{gleason1957} needs dimension three; the lattice version does not, the parallelogram law being granted by the balanced splitter); the multiplicity rule $A = \sum a_i^2$ and the square as the only power are derived, and the cross term $2ab\,\mathcal K(\Delta)$ is forced at the click. Not reached by the algebra: the constants $c_j$, the detector's response to the harmonics of the phase; a single harmonic $j$ is the Born form under the relabelling $p \to jp$, a mixture a different law, the flat mixture the phase-blind detector, which interference excludes (the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 2a; the built click). As $\Nphi$ grows the admissible readings are the same family, the cone of the even positive-definite functions on the circle with odd harmonics only; no $\Nphi$ and no continuity forces $c_j = [j = 1]$, and the fundamental is what the register reads.

\paragraph{Interference, by the formulas alone.} Every phenomenon of this paper is read the same way: Outside, what a detector counts; down to Inside, the rows, their phases, the merge and the evaluation; back Outside, the click's counts over the births against the reading. Two slits: one record is born with two rows of amount $1$, one per opening, $\mathtt m = 2$; each row's phase advances one turn per Link; at pixel $x$ the two arrive with phases $p_1(x)$, $p_2(x)$, their difference $\Delta(x)$ the path difference times the turn; the merge adds them and an equal pair with $\Delta = \Nphi/2$ cancels to no row; the click evaluates the sum and squares it, the offer $R(x) = 512\,[(C[p_1] + C[p_2])^2 + (S[p_1] + S[p_2])^2] = 1024\,(65536 + C[p_1]C[p_2] + S[p_1]S[p_2])$ up to the tables' rounding, proportional to $1 + \cos\Delta(x)$; the rungs $\rung_x$ of Eq.~\eqref{eq:rung} lay the pixels on the ladder, the click is the pixel under which $u$ falls, and over $\Nphi$ births the count at $x$ is $\rung_x - \rung_{x-1}$, Born's to $1/\Nphi$, with the exact tables. With the declared tables at $1/256$ the weights vary with the birth phase within the tables' rounding (hypothesis (a) of Theorem~\ref{th:gleason} holds only to that rounding), so the count over the births departs from the rung difference by up to that rounding: two offers of equal ideal weight at the phases $u$ and $u + 1824$, $\Nphi = 8192$, read $4104$ and $4088$ for $4096$ each, a departure of $8/\Nphi$ (a computation from Eqs.~\eqref{eq:joint} and~\eqref{eq:rung}, not a run); the built click's bound is the tables' rounding, the theorem's $1/\Nphi$ its ideal. The spacing is the law's own: $\lambda = c\Nphi d/n$ Links, one turn of the phase per age per fringe, Young's $\lambda D/s$ only in the paraxial limit (rung 2, the fan) \cite{lightoutside}; the bands' centres are $23.5$ pixels apart for the exact two-path law's $23.3$ (L2b, DETECTOR of the engine before 2026-09-23, history). What passes is a pixel with $\Delta$ near $0$, a wide rung; what does not is a pixel with $\Delta = \Nphi/2$, the rows cancelled, a rung of width $0$ where no click can land; one slit is one row per pixel, nothing cancels, a flat count within the fan's grain and no dark pixel; the Mach-Zehnder's two ports are the same algebra at two Nodes, the bright port $64$ of $64$ clicks and the dark port $0$ (row 2b; Appendix~\ref{app:reproduction}).  

\paragraph{Planck and de Broglie, as identities.} Under the declared dictionary the release's cost rule reads as $E = h_q s = (h_q\Nphi) f$ and the turn rule as $\lambda = h_A/p$: Planck's and de Broglie's relations are identities of the update rules with one constant, $h = h_q\Nphi = h_A$, an input (the forcing ledger \cite{records}); no detector reading of them is registered.

\paragraph{The uncertainty relation.} On the identification of the circle as position and its transform as momentum, a hypothesis of the program and not a derivation (\cite{derivations}, section 22), the support bound $|\mathrm{supp}\,f|\,|\mathrm{supp}\,\hat f| \ge \Nphi$ \cite{donoho1989}, the entropic bound \cite{maassen1988} and Kennard's form $\Delta x\,\Delta p \ge \hbar/2$ in the limit \cite{kennard1927,robertson1929} are the transform's mathematics on $\Z_{\Nphi}$ and nothing of the law; the entropy identity of the click, bits read plus bits not read of $u$ equal to $\log_2 \Nphi$ per record, is an identity of the wheel. What makes it an uncertainty is the one read-out: a record read at a Node gives its position and loses its phase, read on the fan's angle it gives its momentum's direction and not its Node; the same one read-out is what denies Bell a hidden joint distribution (``The one fact and its two faces'', Section~\ref{sec:click}; \cite[section 10]{clickframe}). 

\subsection{Bell and CHSH: from weights to counts}\label{sec:bell}

The correlation at the settings $(a, b)$ is $E =
(c_{++} + c_{--} - c_{+-} - c_{-+})/\Nphi$ over $\Nphi$ births, one per $u$, and
the CHSH sum is $S = E(a, b) - E(a, b') + E(a', b) + E(a', b')$ at the
labels $(0, \Nphi/8, \Nphi/4, 3\Nphi/8)$. Two theorems follow from the
definitions, exact on the GameBoard.

\begin{theorem}[Exact count marginals]\label{th:marginals}
For a pair with labels $\{0, 1\}$ of equal weight and settings $a, b$, let
$J(o_A, o_B) = \sum_\ell U_a[o_A][\ell]\,U_b[o_B][\ell]$ and
$R(o_A, o_B) = J^2$. Then the first party's outcome is $+$ exactly for
$u < \Nphi/2$ and $-$ for $u \ge \Nphi/2$, for every $(a, b)$ and every $\Nphi$; and
the second party's count of $+$ is exactly $\Nphi/2$ for every $(a, b)$ unless
$2\Nphi R(+,+)/C_K$ is an odd integer (a tie of the rung), in which case it is
$\Nphi/2 + 1$. No tie occurs for any setting pair at the twelve grains from $8$ to $1024$ of \cite{checks}, nor at the CHSH labels for any multiple of $8$ up to $4096$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Write $n_a = C'[a]^2 + S'[a]^2$. Since the rows of $U_b$ are orthogonal on
the integers, $\sum_{o_B} J(o_A, o_B)^2 = n_a n_b$ for each $o_A$, so
$C_K = 2n_a n_b$ and the coarse cumulative after the first party's $+$ is
$C_K/2$: $\rung = \lfloor (\Nphi C_K + C_K)/(2C_K)\rfloor = \lfloor (\Nphi+1)/2 \rfloor =
\Nphi/2$. For the second party, $R(o_A, o_B) = R(-o_A, -o_B)$ (the rows of
$U_s$ are each other's quarter turn), so with $x = \Nphi R(+,+)/C_K$ the counts
are $c_{++} = \lfloor x + \tfrac12\rfloor$ and $c_{-+} = \rung_3 - \Nphi/2$ with
$\rung_3 = \lfloor (2\Nphi(C_K - R(+,+)) + C_K)/(2C_K)\rfloor = \Nphi + \lfloor \tfrac12 -
x\rfloor$. Hence $c_{++} + c_{-+} = \Nphi/2 + \lfloor y\rfloor + \lfloor 1 -
y\rfloor$ with $y = x + \tfrac12$, which is $\Nphi/2$ when $y \notin \Z$ and
$\Nphi/2 + 1$ when $y \in \Z$. The tie condition is $2x \in 2\Z + 1$, that
is $2\Nphi R(+,+)/C_K$ odd. The absence of ties at the listed $\Nphi$ is the computation over every setting pair \cite{checks}. \end{proof} No-signalling in the arrival intervals and in the counts: the arrival interval at either arm is that arm's flight alone, independent of the other arm's setting and length (Definition~\ref{def:click}, the flight blind) (that interval the host's tick at the arm's set, GAMEBOARD \cite[record 768]{log}; the arm's own count is read only under the later key \texttt{clock\_stamp}, outside this paper's law); neither party's recorded outcome exists as a row before the completion, whose interval is the last arm's, so the availability of the record, unlike the arrival, waits on the far arm's length, and the paper claims no independence for that latency; the first party's outcome is determined by $u$ at the record's birth (Theorem~\ref{th:marginals}) and the second's at the completion by the joint weights, both written at the completion, with the marginal $\Nphi/2$ for every setting (Theorem~\ref{th:marginals}); so neither the counts nor the arrival times at either arm carry the other arm's setting or length, and the one non-local step of the law (P6) is the assignment of the second party's outcome from the joint weights at the completion, on the labels; its interval, the record's, is the last arm's. What the theorem does not cover, stated here. The wheel of the registered pair worlds runs at the rate $1$ against $\Nphi$, one birth per $u$ in order, so the first party's outcomes over the births are $\Nphi/2$ of $+$ followed by $\Nphi/2$ of $-$, a square wave whose serial correlation over a cycle is $1 - 4/\Nphi$ ($0.9990$ at $4096$), a prediction of the sequence in time that no run reads and no row compares with nature's record of outcomes, which shows no such order. The marginal is for settings fixed or chosen independently of the wheel: a setting chosen from $u$ ($a = 0$ for $u < \Nphi/2$ and $a = \Nphi/2$ after, $b = 0$) gives the second party $+$ at every one of the $64$ births at $\Nphi = 64$. On the register the settings are declared per world or balanced over every $u$ (the choosers' $960$ births meet every $u$ with every pair once), so nothing chooses a setting from $u$; nature's freedom-of-choice loophole has its counterpart here in the wheel, not closed by the register, and the reading that would test it is a marginal off $\Nphi/2$ with the settings chosen from $u$ \cite{criteria}. And the order of the second party's outcomes carries the first party's settings even when they are independent of the wheel: the ladder's cells give $B = A$ at $a = b$ and $B = -A$ at $a = b + \Nphi/2$ exactly, so with $b = 0$ a first party keeping $a = 0$ leaves the second a serial correlation $\langle B_tB_{t+1}\rangle = 15/16$ over $192$ births at $\Nphi = 64$, and one cycling $a = \Nphi/2, 0, 0$ (the period $3$, coprime to $\Nphi$, the independence criterion above) leaves $-5/16$, the marginal $96/96$ in both, the same at every shift of the wheel and of the chooser (a computation from the theorem's cells, not a run): the second party reads one bit of the first's choice from the order of its own outcomes. So the theorem's no-signalling is of the counts over a cycle and of the arrival times; the sequence in time signals under the sequential wheel, a result of the law as built and a FAIL of any claim beyond the counts, open until the wheel is other than a counter (P4 allows no draw; the declared form below is a permutation from a world input, not a draw), or the claim is kept to the counts, as it is here. Stated plainly: the law as built, with its sequential wheel, does not meet operational no-signalling; its counts are blind to the other party's setting, the order of its outcomes is not, and until the wheel is other than a counter the pair's construction models a Bell experiment in its counts only, not in its record of outcomes. The declared form (2026-09-24, \cite[record 1647]{log}): the births of the pair record take the residues of $\Z_{\Nphi}$, one per $u$, in an order set by the world's seed through a declared integer hash (a Fisher--Yates permutation under a 64-bit SplitMix64 mixing hash) in place of the counter's $[1, 1]$; the click is stamped with the detector's count and the birth interval, never $u$; the seed is an input of kind 1 drawn once per world, never read Outside and independent of the settings; the lamp's cadence is fixed and independent of the residues; the click's stamp is the cell's own first rung, never the completion tick. Stated honestly: the nonlocality is Inside and declared, one gather; the model's standing is Bohm's under quantum equilibrium \cite{bohm1952,dgz1992}; no reader Outside without the seed beats $1/2$. Row 1c's cell stands as derived under the counter until the declared form's runs are read. The order channel's width at $b = 3N/8$ equals the finite-$N$ correlation $E_N$ exactly ($1448/2048 = 181/256 = S_N/4$), a closed form and not a statistic; the birth residue $u$ is a hidden variable known at both stations, the birth stamp travelling with the record, so the counter form of the click is a deterministic hidden-variable model, and Bell's theorem forces its nonlocality into the order of outcomes, one way, from the first party to the second (the second's rung computed from $R(o_A, o_B)$ with $a$ and $o_A$ supplied), which nature's quantum mechanics does not carry: the counter form's own falsifiable departure from nature, declared before any run \cite{orderderivation}. Read after a detector on the registered pair world of the engine before 2026-09-23, history (the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 1c): the second party's serial correlation $15/16$ under a constant setting and $-1/16$ under the period-$3$ cycle $0, 21, 42$ (the cycle $\Nphi/2, 0, 0$ the register's keys cannot declare; the declarable cycle reads the same channel with a smaller swing), the marginals $96/96$ under both, the algebra met at $16$ of $16$ checks, nature's value $0$: FAIL \cite{orderchannel}.

The strict-crossing rung $\Nphi C_k > uC_K$ would give the second party $33/64$ in $3944$ of the $4096$ setting pairs at $\Nphi = 64$, a signalling of $1/\Nphi$ made by the rounding \cite{design}; the nearest rung is what the theorem needs. The theorem's scope is what it states:
a pair of two labels with equal weights, the CHSH form, and the rung of
\eqref{eq:rung}; unequal weights and more than two labels are not covered,
and no-signalling for them is open. That the marginal at $B$ is $\Nphi/2$ for every $a$ although $B$'s rung is computed from $R(o_A, o_B)$ with $a$ and $o_A$ supplied by the layer (Definition~\ref{def:click}) is the content of the theorem; the joint counts are not local, and the model does not claim they are.



\begin{theorem}[The finite-$\Nphi$ Bell value]\label{th:bell}
With the counts of Theorem~\ref{th:marginals} and off a tie,
$E_{\Nphi}(a, b) = 4c_{++}/\Nphi - 1$ and
\begin{equation}
\bigl|E_{\Nphi}(a, b) - \cos(2\pi(a-b)/\Nphi)\bigr| \le \frac{2}{\Nphi} + 4\arcsin\frac{\sqrt2}{2\varrho} < \frac{2}{\Nphi} + 0.0111,\qquad \varrho = N_t - \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2},
\label{eq:ebound}
\end{equation}
so at the labels $(0, \Nphi/8, \Nphi/4, 3\Nphi/8)$, $|S(\Nphi) - 2\sqrt2| \le 8/\Nphi + 0.0444$.
$S(\Nphi)$ is an exact rational for each $\Nphi$; it lies above $2\sqrt2$ for
$252$ of the $512$ multiples of $8$ up to $4096$ (among them $\Nphi = 16, 32$
with $S = 3$ and $\Nphi = 128$ with $S = 23/8$) and equals $181/64 = 2.828125$ at every power of two from $512$ through $8192$ and $5793/2048 = 2.828613$ at $16384$ \cite{checks}; measured after a detector at $512$, $1024$, $2048$, $4096$, $8192$ and $16384$ \cite{register} (the $S(\Nphi)$ figure of the engine before 2026-09-23, history \cite{records}).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$c_{++} = \lfloor x + \tfrac12\rfloor$ with $x = \Nphi R(+,+)/C_K$ gives
$|c_{++} - x| \le \tfrac12$ and $E_{\Nphi} = 4c_{++}/\Nphi - 1$ from the mirror
symmetry, so $|E_{\Nphi} - (4R(+,+)/C_K - 1)| \le 2/\Nphi$. The vector
$(C'[s], S'[s])$ differs from $256(\cos\theta_s, \sin\theta_s)$,
$\theta_s = \pi s/\Nphi$, by at most $\tfrac12$ per component, so its
direction differs from $\theta_s$ by at most $\delta = \arcsin(\sqrt2/(2\varrho))$
with $\varrho = N_t - \sqrt2/2 = 255.29$, below every table vector's length
(each component within $\tfrac12$ of $256\cos$ or $256\sin$), so
$4\delta = 0.01108 < 0.0111$ and $16\delta = 0.04432 < 0.0444$;
$J(+,+)/\sqrt{n_a n_b}$ is the cosine of the angle between the two
directions, $\cos(\theta_a - \theta_b + \epsilon)$ with $|\epsilon| \le
2\delta$, and $4R(+,+)/C_K - 1 = 2\cos^2(\cdot) - 1 = \cos(2(\theta_a -
\theta_b) + 2\epsilon)$, within $4\delta$ of $\cos(2\pi(a-b)/\Nphi)$. The
four settings add the bounds. The values of $S(\Nphi)$ are the computation
from these formulas with the repository's tables \cite{checks}, which
reproduces the design's $176/64$, $720/256$ and $2896/1024$ at $\Nphi = 64,
256, 1024$ and the engine's three values below.
\end{proof}

What Theorem~\ref{th:bell} does not say: that $S(\Nphi) \le 2\sqrt2$, false for about half the $\Nphi$; nor that the deficit is $O(1/\Nphi)$ from below. The tables' term in \eqref{eq:ebound} is the resolution $1/256$ of the circle's tables and does not shrink with $\Nphi$; at the CHSH labels the tables' entries are the same at every $\Nphi$, so the rounding gives $181/64$ at the powers of two from $512$ through $8192$ and $5793/2048 = 2.828613$ at $16384$ and $32768$ (measured at $16384$, DETECTOR), and beyond the tables' bound $2\Nphi \le 65536$ the rungs on the fixed correlations are the closed form $\boxed{S(\Nphi) = 8(c_1 + c_1')/\Nphi - 4}$ with $c_1$, $c_1'$ the ladder's first cell's counts, whose limit with the tables fixed is $186034/65773 = 2.828425$, $2.1 \times 10^{-6}$ below $2\sqrt2$; $2\sqrt2$ is the joint limit in $\Nphi$ and $N_t$ \cite{checks,register}. At a tie $c_{--} = c_{++} - 1$ and $E_{\Nphi}$ drops by $2/\Nphi$; no tie occurs at the CHSH labels up to $4096$.

\paragraph{The finite-grain value, and what would make it a prediction.} The construction's number is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prediction}
\boxed{\,S_{\mathrm{U24}} = \frac{181}{64} = 2.828125 \ \text{exactly}, \qquad
\Delta S = S_{\mathrm{U24}} - 2\sqrt2 = -3.02 \times 10^{-4}\,},
\end{equation}
at every power of two from $512$ through $8192$, with the tables at
$N_t = 256$, the wheel at $N_u = \Nphi$, the settings $(0, \Nphi/8, \Nphi/4,
3\Nphi/8)$ and a pair of two labels with equal weights; the marginals
exactly $1/2$; the correlations at the two pairs of settings
$725/1024$ and $723/1024$ at $\Nphi = 4096$, above and below $1/\sqrt2$;
$5793/2048$ at $16384$ and $32768$. It was computed in advance and measured after a detector at $\Nphi = 512$, $2048$, $4096$, $8192$ and, the plateau's end, $16384$ (the last three \cite[at b34fe114]{register}; the $S(\Nphi)$ figure of the engine before 2026-09-23, history \cite{records}), under the click and the wheel with every pin met (the register's block of the derivation's 24.4); $512$ and $4096$ were re-run by the second runner \cite{replications}. The criterion: the law at a grain
is rejected when a measured $S$ differs from $S(\Nphi)$ by more than
five standard errors, under the identification of the experiment's
settings and detection with the labels and the ideal read-out, which the model does not model; the comparison with nature is Section~\ref{sec:checks}. It is a prediction of the law only once the pair's wheel meets no-signalling in the order of the outcomes (above), which the sequential wheel as built does not; until then it is the exact consequence of the declared construction at its grain.

\section{The GameBoard: the way the algebra is computed with}\label{sec:gameboard}

The GameBoard is the way the algebra is computed with, not the object: a system of information transfer with costs, read in two ways, the detector's click a measurement and the host's view a diagnostic. This section states the law as one map with its postulates, the state it acts on under the record kinds of Sections~\ref{sec:algebra} and~\ref{sec:massive}, the six operations as the engine runs them, the read-out, the code and the ledger; every sentence is the algebra document's \cite[chapters 2, 3 and 8]{algebra}. The law as the engine ran it before 2026-09-23, the rows that hop whole with their wheel, their rungs and their components, is its record \cite{records}.

\subsection{The law and its implementation}\label{sec:law}

\paragraph{The one map.} The law is the map of Eq.~\eqref{eq:map} applied at every Node at every interval, per component $s$ of the state vector, each with its declared rate $r$ and wall $d$: the component is translated by its rate, counted in walls, capped at $a = 1$ where a cap is declared and uncapped elsewhere (the whole part $\lfloor |s|/d \rfloor$ with the sign), and reduced by the walls it holds; every wall counted is an event, and nothing else happens. One declared variant of the count, the centred step, takes the nearest whole number the accumulator holds, $(|s| + \lfloor d/2 \rfloor)$ divided by $d$ with the sign; it is named where a rule uses it. Where the rate is a constant of the world (the linear block) every component has the closed form $s(t) = \lfloor s_0 + rt \rfloor$, $r$ the rate as a fraction of the wall, so a record's state at any interval is a formula of its birth and its age; where the rate is a function of what arrives (the feedback block: the push, the drive, the coupling of the two kinds) the map is iterated and its continuum limit is the differential equation $d\mathbf s/dt = \mathbf r(\mathbf s)$. The read-out is one comparison, the click \cite[chapter 2]{algebra}.

\paragraph{Rules, parameters, initial conditions.} The law is stated as rules, apart from the parameters and the initial conditions a world supplies. The rules: (P1) every quantity of the state is a bounded integer and every operation integer arithmetic, no real number, root or floating point at run time; (P2) space is a cubic array of Nodes, each joined to six neighbours by Links through directional Ports, a Node's complete local information its NodeState, time a sequence of intervals; (P3) the rates and walls of the map are made of the six operations of Section~\ref{sec:intro} and nothing else; (P4) a rule reads its own record and the six neighbours; nothing is kept at a Node beyond the events there, no register or draw, and the remainder $r$ of Eq.~\eqref{eq:massive} is a component of the record's own state (the pair travels with the record \cite[8.8]{algebra}), not a register at the Node; (P5) no row or body crosses more than one Link per interval; (P6) a record is read out once, by one comparison, at the click, the one step that deletes, and the click of a pair is one gather of one record from both settings, the law's one non-local operation. Beside P6, once: the pair is one record with two arms (Definition~\ref{def:click}, the record $\psi = (00) + (11)$ of rank $2$, each arm carrying the weights, nothing of one arm written on the other); the completion is one gather at the completion interval, no interval crosses between the arms and no arm's history is altered; the counts' no-signalling follows from the table's symmetry (Theorem~\ref{th:marginals}); the completion is an operation of the law that relaxes P4 at that one step only, said so and not hidden. The parameters (P7, P8): the circle $\Nphi$ and its tables at $1/256$, the pair $[\mathrm{num}, \mathrm{den}]$ of each record kind with its pitch, light the value $[1, 1]$ (Eq.~\eqref{eq:massive}), the rung $W$ of each detector, the cells of each block with its lowered pair, the take of each absorbing object, and the roundings declared at load; the initial conditions: the box and its boundaries, the blocks with their momenta, the lamps and the detectors of the world file, and the seed, the bound mode's integer profile over the whole board, the engine reading integers \cite[8.7]{algebra}. The law of this paper is the runtime at the commit Appendix~\ref{app:reproduction} names. The rules chosen among few (P9) are assumptions, not derivations, each named where it enters and each marked in the algebra document as carried, proved or computed and not proved: the rule with the pair per kind, carried from the design, its band and its two paces proved; the click's definition at the rung, carried on the author's word; the one formula of a block's motion, carried from the continuum, its two limits proved; the stress of light at a block's outer Ports as the wave's momentum flux, the design's declaration; and the bijection of the interval, the design's proof carried (Section~\ref{sec:massive}). One axiom of the apparatus (P10): the click stores one pointer per set, the least-rank member of the family Theorem~\ref{th:gleason} forces, which is Born's form with the fundamental harmonic; which harmonic is a relabelling of the declared rate, and the harmonic constants are not derived. One assumption of the frame (P11): the GameBoard, Inside, is read only through its emitters and detectors, Outside; every result Outside is a click, a number of the board's state is never a reading, and every comparison with experiment is a comparison of clicks with readings; a measurement is itself an event of the board, an emitter putting a record on it and a detector ending the record at the click, the one step that deletes Inside and the one row that Outside gains. Nothing outside this list is assumed.

\paragraph{The state.} The GameBoard is a box of Nodes in $\Z^3$, each joined to six neighbours by Links through six Ports, an axis periodic or open; time is the interval $t \in \Z$; the state at an interval is a vector $\mathbf s$ of bounded integers on a product of circles and lines. A Node's complete local information is its NodeState: per record kind present, the record's row, its two levels and its remainder $(a_{\mathrm{now}}, a_{\mathrm{before}}, r)$ of Eq.~\eqref{eq:massive}; at a block's cell, the block's lowered pair, its pointer in the units of the conserved form and its count; nothing else, no register, no draw, no field beyond the records there \cite[2.11, 8.1, 8.6]{algebra}. A block carries its cells, its momentum $\mathbf p$ in $\Z^3$ and its step's accumulator per axis with its remainder (Section~\ref{sec:massive}). The rows that hop, a tuple (Node, direction, age, phase, emitter, content, record, label, amount, multiplicity) moving one Link per interval on a digital line, are the engine as built before 2026-09-23, kept as their record \cite[2.11]{algebra}: Definition~\ref{def:row} and the theorems stated on them (Theorems~\ref{th:isometry}, \ref{th:bijection}, \ref{th:gleason}, \ref{th:marginals} and~\ref{th:bell}) stand as proved, on the objects they name.

\paragraph{The six operations as the engine runs them.} One interval applies, in order, (T) on every accumulator; (D), whose whole part is the event; (B) at the push and at the click; (G) and (E) where records are summed at one Node and where they end; and (P) at a collision \cite[2.11]{algebra}. In symbols, one line each \cite[2.1 to 2.6]{algebra}: (T) $x \mapsto x + r$ on $\Z^k$ or on the torus, every count of the law, the translation group of the torus this verb on Nodes; (B) a moment sum over the neighbourhood's records, $\mathbf u^{\mathsf T}\mathbf C\mathbf v$ with $\mathbf C$ declared, the push's rate bilinear in the state, the click's weight $\mathbf f^{\mathsf T}\mathbf G\mathbf f$ with $\mathbf G = \mathbf E^{\mathsf T}\mathbf E$ this form on the record's element, nothing squared as a step of its own; (G) the merge $f \mapsto f + g$ in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$ with the cancel $[p + \Nphi/2] = -[p]$, the quotient by $x^{\Nphi/2} + 1$, which for $\Nphi$ a power of two is the ring of cyclotomic integers $\Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$, a free $\Z$-module of rank $\Nphi/2$, two arms' elements multiplying by the ring's convolution; (P) a permutation of directions, labels or Nodes, never of contents (a gate, a tie); (E) the exact evaluation $\mathrm{ev} : \Z[\Z_{\Nphi}] \to \Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$, a surjective ring homomorphism whose kernel is the ideal of the cancel, so that $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]/\ker \mathrm{ev} = \Z[\zeta_{\Nphi}]$ exactly, and beside it the built evaluation, the tables at the scale $256$, a $\Z$-linear map into $\Z^2$ that is not a ring homomorphism, its kernel larger than the cancel's (at $\Nphi = 64$, $\mathbf E(e_1)^2 = (64400, 12750)$ against $256\,\mathbf E(e_2) = (64256, 12800)$, COMPUTATION), the exact line the algebra's and the rounding the engine's declared constant; (D) the signed truncating division with the remainder kept in $(-d, d)$, the code's wording in force, the Euclidean division on every non-negative accumulator, and the comparison as part of the verb, a division whose quotient is $0$ or $1$ and whose remainder is not read. What is not one of the six: a root of the state at run time, the seventh verb, not admitted, which Lorentz's gamma on a body's own counter would need (Section~\ref{sec:click}); a rounded constant multiplying a record in flight is a declared rounding at load, not a verb; no float, no true division, no draw \cite[2.7]{algebra}.

\paragraph{The three tests, rule by rule.} A rule enters the law only if it is generic (one primitive with declared integers, no family name or kind, the engine branching on no name), vector (one of the six verbs on the state vector, its rate at most bilinear in the state, no root, no float, no rounding at run time beyond the ones declared at load) and local (its own record and the six neighbouring Nodes, fixed work and storage for a fixed $K$, nothing kept at a Node); generic means commuting with the $48$ \cite[2.8]{algebra}. Each rule of Section~\ref{sec:massive} passes the three and carries its mark \cite[8.10]{algebra}: the rule with the pair on the six reads, (B), (T) and (D), the band and the two paces proved, the range-one bound computed and not proved; the conserved form, a bilinear form of the two levels, proved on every board with the remainders' identity; the well of the pair on declared cells, the threshold and the tail computed and not proved, light's norm bound proved; the motion, the one formula carried, its two limits proved; the coupling, (B) linear in the other kind's two columns and one (D) per row, the Euler--Lagrange scheme and the invariant $J$ with its remainder identity proved, the index and the pump computed and not proved; the click across the block's cells at $W$, (E), the bilinear form and (D)'s comparison, the definition carried; the take, a declaration, no identity; the seed, the standing start proved; the direction of time, (D) with the ceiling, the bijection carried and its inverse exact; the block's momentum, step and push, the cadence and the bound proved as identities of the accumulator, the stress carried as the design's declaration; the force between two blocks through light, the closed form carried, on the GameBoard computed and not proved.

\paragraph{The read-out.} The click is the evaluation (E) of a body's own record on its cells at the declared rung $W$: light arriving at the block's cells drives the block's record through the coupling, the block's pointer accumulates its own record's motion across all its cells in the units of the conserved form, and the click is the comparison $W \times (\text{the pointer}) \ge (\text{the record's norm})$, integers both, in the block's own clock; the click line carries the block's own count and the light record's birth stamp. Light clicks only at a detector set, a declared set of Nodes with its rung $W$; at a massive body's cells light does not click but drives the body's record through the coupling, and the body's own click reads that; a free Node has no rung, no count and no reading; the verbs are lossless, light passes on, and the click needs no sink; where a world must absorb it declares a take, a damping pair on light's row at the cells of an object declared absorbing, a declaration of the world and not the law's \cite[8.6]{algebra}. A click is an action, not a passive read: the record ends at the detector, its content enters the detector's own record, and the detector's count advances, the click stamped with that count \cite[3.1]{algebra}. Between a birth and a click the interval is a bijection, its inverse exact (Section~\ref{sec:massive}, the direction of time; for the rows that hop, Theorem~\ref{th:bijection}); the click is the one deletion, and the pair's gather the one non-local step (P6).

\paragraph{The code as the law's runtime.} Every registered world is run from its world file with its pin written before the run and its source fingerprint (Appendix~\ref{app:reproduction}); the books balance at every interval in every run. The design's scripts, each printing its record beside the design and none an engine run, compute the band and the corner, the conserved forms $I$ and $J$ with their remainders' terms, the block's threshold, the board's margin, the index, the self-trapping of light, the block's clock in motion, the layer and the moving pins, the light clock's relay, the moving index, the well's spectrum and the time reversal \cite[8.10]{algebra}; what they compute and do not prove is marked so above. These are gates on the code, not measurements; the replications and the hand-worked update of the engine before 2026-09-23 are its record \cite{records}.

\paragraph{The ledger.} The forcing ledger, in the paper's records file \cite{records}, is the paper's spine:
for every result, the rules of Eq.~\eqref{eq:map} it starts from, the
assumptions added beside them with their kind, the freedom left, and
the ground of the derivation \cite[2026-09-22]{highlights}: exact on the GameBoard (no limit, no
average), a limit of the grain taken on paper with a rate, or a limit
under a spatial condition, an average that covers the shell (over the
shell's Nodes, over the directions of a fan declared in a ball, or over
the sweep of an orbit), the condition then part of the claim. A result
whose only reading is of the GameBoard's state is not in the table, and a result resting on a hypothesis beside the law or conjectured from the algebra stands in it only with that ground named in its row (the bending's coefficient, conjectured); the hypotheses beside the law are on the tree (Section~\ref{sec:click}).



\section{How the algebra was reached: from the GameBoard to the group}\label{sec:route}

The order of this paper is not the order of the finding. The object of Section~\ref{sec:algebra} was reached from the GameBoard: from one Node and its six neighbours, one message per Link per interval, through the simulator's runs, in dated steps; what did not converge to the group and the ring was not put in. This section states the one choice and what it forces (the algebra document's chapter 7 \cite{algebra}), the road from the operations to the group, the dated steps, the platform on which a formula is arrived at by two roads, and the check of the roads; the two direction tables, the simulator's part and the dictionary of the rows that hop, as the paper carried them, are its record \cite{records}.

\paragraph{The one choice, and the seven Nodes.} The one choice of the model is the six Ports of a Node, $P = \{\pm x, \pm y, \pm z\}$ with the opposite involution, the $L^1$ neighbourhood of the cubic lattice: a Node and its six neighbours, the seven Nodes of the causal front, one message per Link per interval in each direction (Section~\ref{sec:algebra}). Two more choices, and no fourth: the phase circle $\Z_{\Nphi}$, $\Nphi$ per world, and the translation group of the torus, $\Z_X \times \Z_Y \times \Z_Z$, each factor a circle or a segment; the point group is then forced and is already the largest, the translation group is the board, and the only freedom that changes the physics is the neighbourhood, through the front, $c$ and the tables \cite[chapter 7]{algebra}.

\paragraph{What the choice forces: the $48$, and the $24$ within them.} What is not chosen is the group of $48$: every map that preserves the six Ports as a set and the lattice's Links is one of the signed permutations of the three axes, $3! \times 2^3 = 48$, and every one of them does; no three-dimensional lattice has a point group of order above $48$ \cite[chapter 7]{algebra}, and the cubic lattice's is the full octahedral group of that order, so this lattice keeps the $48$ and no more. Nothing was added to it: the mass, the charge and the other contents of the family table live on the amounts, on which the $48$ act trivially. The only $\Z$-linear bijections that preserve the cone of one Link per interval are these $48$; a boost is not $\Z$-linear, so no boost is among them, and Lorentz's form is reached Outside from the clicks (Section~\ref{sec:click}) and not as a symmetry of the lattice. The determinant splits the $48$: the $24$ rotations, the group of order $24$, isomorphic to $S_4$ on the cube's four body diagonals, and the $24$ reflections; the hand, needed to carry spin and polarisation, is the pseudoscalar that tells them apart, $h \mapsto \det(g)\,h$ (Theorem~\ref{th:group}); the $24$ are the octahedron's rotations, not a numeral chosen. The GameBoard showed that everything converges to this group and this ring, and what did not converge was not put in (the author's sentence, record 1109 \cite{log}).

\paragraph{From the operations to the group.} The operations did not deduce a group; they came first, as acts on the board: a row flies one Link per interval along its direction, rows meet at a Node, a body steps by an accumulator against a wall, a phase turns, identical rows merge, a detector clicks; each was then written as one of the six operations on a state vector. The group is the answer to which maps preserve what the operations act on, a Node of six Ports and its Links and a cone of one Link per interval: the bijections of the Ports that keep opposite Ports opposite are the $48$ signed permutations, and they are the only $\Z$-linear bijections that preserve the cone, a boost being not $\Z$-linear, so Lorentz's form is reached Outside from the clicks and not as a symmetry of the lattice (Section~\ref{sec:click}). The $48$ first appeared in the code as the invariance of one operation, the collision's table, and were recognised after as the symmetry of all of them; the $24$ came from the hand, the pseudoscalar that carrying spin and polarisation needed, which $\det(g)$ keeps or flips. The other objects came the same way: the step and the flight are shifts, hence the translation group; the turn adds modulo $\Nphi$, hence $\Z_{\Nphi}$, and the merge of records is the addition of $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$; the collision is a permutation of a finite set; and $c$ was not chosen, it is the flight operator's norm. What the group does back is to force forms: a rule that reads only the local state is required to commute with the $48$ (the P-rule, a requirement beyond locality), and the symmetric integer matrices fixed by the $48$ are the multiples of the identity, so the only isotropic quadratic reading of a body's momentum within the six operations is $c\,\mathbf p \cdot \mathbf p$, and the square $W$ of Eq.~\eqref{eq:square} is assembled from three things derived separately, the $48$ forcing the form's isotropy (every quadratic invariant a multiple of $\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf p$), the $3$ the chain's $1/c^2 = 3$ and $E_0'^2$ the band's bottom; ``generic'' in the three tests of every rule means exactly this. The definitions and this road, with their code and tests, are the group-structure page of the tree \cite{groupstructure}; this paper writes no second definition.

\paragraph{The transition from ordinary physics to the algebra, dated.} The twenty-four dated steps, each a thing of physics becoming an object of the law with the reading that showed it, are \cite{history} (\texttt{docs/designs/algebra\_transition/HISTORY.md} on \texttt{main} at 412f5c61), their dates once: 2026-09-17 the shared resource deleted and the amplitude a phase with a content; 09-18 the Born table from $\Nphi$ and a Node its six Ports; 09-19 the quantum an integer row, the click the one border, the push one bilinear form, $E = hf$ a release's cost; 09-20 the readings by kind, the masses the initialisation, every count an accumulator, the fan a width of the law; 09-21 the six verbs, the record in $\Z[\Z_{\Nphi}]$, the lattice the translation group, the Lorentz factor refused as a seventh verb; 09-22 the detector's clock, the click theorem and the framing. 

\paragraph{The platform: how a formula is arrived at, by the algebra and by the simulator.} Every formula of this paper is arrived at on one platform, by two roads that meet at the detector. The algebraic road has three steps. The Inside step: the six verbs on the record's attributes, the family's declared integers naming which attributes the step reads (Section~\ref{sec:law}; the families table \cite{records}). The conversion: an emitter puts a record on the board and a detector ends it at a click, so that Outside there are counts and Nodes only, the detector's own count the age wall's member at coefficient $1$ (P11). The Outside form: a ratio or a difference of those counts, the image of the Inside step, with its rung (exact, in the fan's limit, in the shell mean) and its order in the grain; a known form, Einstein's or Young's, stands on the comparison side only. The simulator's road runs the same three steps: a world file declares the families, the emitters and the detectors, and the reading is pinned before the run. Every reading of the simulator's road is DETECTOR in its count (each series with its detector in the conversion table \cite{records}), the self-creations' ticks of series S GAMEBOARD; where a count is taken at an open-face detector without a body (the redshift rows 3, 4b and 12) it is read at head in the detector's own clock, its count of self-creations under the age wall ($r = 1.0000$, no crowd at the detector; \cite{criteria}, the re-run of 2026-09-22), equal to the host's interval to the integer, DETECTOR; the registered run's time base was the host's interval \cite[record 768]{log}, superseded; a two-way light clock at the detector, not read, reads the same count in no crowd (series X); and a number of the board's state is a diagnostic, never a reading. A formula enters the paper with both roads: the algebra's chain with its inputs and its word (the roads table \cite{records}), the simulator's reading with its series and kind (the conversion table \cite{records} and the $S(\Nphi)$ figure of the engine before 2026-09-23, history \cite{records}), and nature on the comparison side (the full record \cite{nature,records}). The platform is the paper's offer beyond its list: to arrive at a further formula, declare the family and the attributes it reads, write the Inside step on them, name the detector and what it counts, take the ratio Outside, pin it before the run, and read it by kind; the three chains below do this in full.

\paragraph{The road to each, and the check that nothing was derived from them.} The three roads are the one chain above, each from the Inside step, the six verbs, (A1) and, where it enters, (A2), with (A3), locality Outside (nothing Outside passes faster than a chain of clicks or jumps a Node), a definition of Outside and not a law \cite{einsteinoutside}: to Lorentz, the boost from two legs at one Node per interval with $k_{AB} = k_{BA}$, the scale $r$ free until (A2) fixes it at $\sqrt{1 - v^2}$ (the click frame's section 2); to Einstein, the rate $1/\gamma$ as $r$ read from two factors and $E^2 = E_0^2 + c^2p^2$ as the line of the rate with $W$ shown to second order (Theorems 1 and 2 and rows II.1, II.3 and II.6 of \cite{einsteinoutside}); to the step above itself, the Outside step as the image of the Inside step, Einstein's step its most general form where $r$ is supplied, its quantum a theorem of (A1), (A3) and the drive's one Link per self-creation, Newton's step its limit at $v \ll c$ (section 3 of \cite{einsteinoutside}). Einstein's, Lorentz's and the Outside step's formulas appear in these chains only as the thing compared with; no chain takes them as an input, and the Outside step is never a second formula set beside the Inside step. The word is ``follows'' or ``recovered'' where a known form is arrived at, ``shown to second order'' for $W$ under (A1) and (A2), ``declared'' for $W$ on the rows' dynamics and for the unit $E_0 = mc^2$; ``derived'' stands nowhere. the roads table \cite{records} (the paper's records file \cite{records}) lists the check row by row, the inputs, the file and line where each chain starts and the word, read against the certification tables of the two sources and audited in their review.

\section{The comparison with nature, and the failures by cause}\label{sec:comparison}

Everything compared here is a detector's count or a ratio of counts (Section~\ref{sec:click}); the readings are compared by kind, and each failure is named with its cause.

\subsection{The simulator's checks and the comparison with nature}\label{sec:checks}

Three things are kept apart: the gates on the code; what is shown Inside by algebra under named assumptions, which needs no experiment; and what is measured, a run Inside read Outside, compared with known experiments.

\paragraph{The formulas after a detector.} Every number read after a detector is a count of clicks or a click's tick at a declared detector, registered with its source fingerprint (Appendix~\ref{app:reproduction}; \cite{register,replications}), its expectation written before the run; a number of the GameBoard's state appears nowhere. Seven formulas shown Inside (the pace, the click's power, Mach-Zehnder, the marginals, GHZ, Malus, light beside a mass) were confirmed by their runs on the engine before 2026-09-23, history (Appendix~\ref{app:reproduction}); the readings that no formula gives are the conversion table's \cite{records} (the clock's field at two Nodes, the equivalence after a detector, the covariant readings) and the $S(\Nphi)$ figure's, history \cite{records} ($S$ at seven grains).





\paragraph{The method.} An experiment is a world file: the GameBoard's extents, the blocks placed on it as the bodies of the experiment, the lamps and the detectors, every one a declared object of Section~\ref{sec:massive}; a result is clicks, a count between clicks on a detector's own record or a ratio of such counts; the pin, the number the algebra gives, is written before the run and no pin moves after a reading. Every row of the paper's list passes three checks in order \cite{approvals}: approved in the algebra, its number following from the one law before any run and closed on the closure page \cite{closure}; approved on the GameBoard without pins, an exploratory run reading beside the algebra's number within the band the physicist declared, labelled exploratory and never a result; approved with pins, the pin written before the run \cite{declarations,schedule}, one run on a recorded decision, the clicks read by the reader of record and the reading by kind inside the pin. A row is (K), a known-formula row whose algebraic identity is a textbook formula and whose engine reading is the control of the engine against the algebra, or (P), a prediction row, a number the algebra gives and no known formula gives; a prediction is not a pass. A reading that falls outside its pin is written as a miss, in this table, by kind; every number of the law is stated as matching nature or not, never as how nature is. Table~\ref{tab:list} is the paper's list at this version: every pinned reading is a blank, since no row of the list has yet been read on the engine as it stands, and the blanks fill as each run is read and merged; the old comparison of the engine before 2026-09-23, its rows, its readings and its figures, is history in the records file \cite{records}, never carried into this table.



\paragraph{The limitations, stated before the comparison.} The third status follows from the structure of the law as built and never from the outcome, and a referee's test that every cell of the table must pass is that a row sits in the same class had it agreed. The law as built derives a moving clock's rate, $1/\gamma_m$ at the massive kind's cone (Section~\ref{sec:massive}), and not the Lorentz group: the GameBoard is a medium with a rest frame, Lorentz's symmetry belongs to the limit and to the clicks, no Michelson--Morley or Kennedy--Thorndike row is claimed, and the light clock in motion is a predicted FAIL as declared (row LCm); the beam law's bodies that hop had $r = 1$ at every speed and nothing contracted, no relativistic dynamics on them, history; it has no term of the crowd's history, so no observable that reads the growth of an emitter's stretch with the flight time is predicted; and a declared input is not a prediction, so an observable whose number is a declared give (row 7a), a declared content (row 8c) or a declared coefficient (row 13's $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$) is not predicted, whatever the declared world reads. A fan of directions bounded in Manhattan length is not a fan of every direction (its angular density is the octahedron's, the axes $2.8$ times denser than the face diagonals); a reading that assumes the isotropic mean holds only where the fan is declared uniform in angle at a grain finer than the reading, or where a click read the crowd; otherwise the law's own number for that world is the integral on the comb (the register's finding under rows 6, 10, 13 and 14). The weight rule, stated once: under the declaration $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} > 0$ a moving body's gravitational charge is the pair $w = \gamma_L(1 + \gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}v^2)M$ with its wall, $\gamma_L$ the Lorentz factor of the body's speed and $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ the declared space-curvature coefficient (the parametrized post-Newtonian gamma), declared as that key's rule (decision B, record 1150 \cite{log}); at $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} = 0$ a body weighs $M$, the law's rule at rest, no velocity term on the body; rows 13 and 14 are read under that declaration where they say so, and the coefficient $2(1 + \gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}})$ of row 13 is the declared input and not a result. The count: the paper's list of Table~\ref{tab:list} is closed in the algebra before any run, every pinned reading a blank until its run is read and merged, and none is read yet on the engine as it stands; the old count of the engine before 2026-09-23 is history \cite{records}; the disagreeing rows are the law's own results, and the paper claims no rule it has not shown. Two placements, row 7a to not predicted and row 2a to NOT COMPARED, were decided on 2026-09-23 after the kind audit \cite{kindaudit}; nothing else moved. A row whose apparatus table is the declared law (the polariser's and the splitter's tables) is checked as an implementation of that table, and only a row whose evidence class is DERIVED\_BLIND is offered as a prediction; the class column of Table~\ref{tab:list} fills from the closure page and not from this paper's judgement.

\paragraph{The derivations, final.} Four numbers of the list are the algebra's identities and stand whatever the runs read: Born's exponent $2$ exactly, the click a quadratic form (row 2c); Tsirelson's value $2\sqrt2$ as the limit of the finite-grain Bell value, the local bound beside it (row 1a); $c^2 = 1/3$, the pace of light as the norm of the flight operator, one Link per interval on every line and $1/\sqrt3$ in the Euclidean mean (row 5a); and the rest energy of a massive kind, $h\omega_0$ with $\omega_0 = mc^2$ in the law's units at the massive cone, de Broglie's internal clock as the thing compared with (row M2).

\paragraph{Under the hypothesis, after the pins, on a recorded decision.} Three rows enter only under the pair-field hypothesis, a third record kind sourced by every block's content and read by every Node as its own pair, outside the law under its own identity and never in the list's place: the clock in a field at $r$ and $2r$, the ratio $2.00$ (row 12, Newton's potential from the lattice Green's function); the delay of a light pulse through a medium block sitting in the field, Shapiro's form with the same $1 + \gamma$, one declared input (in place of row 13's bending); and Newton's fall, a prediction of the form and not a pinned row (in place of row 14's orbit).

\paragraph{The rows that left the list.} Under the law as it stands the following rows of the register are not predicted, each with its missing piece named on the schedule \cite{schedule}, and their earlier readings are history in the records file \cite{records}: the far lamp (rows 3 and 11a to 11c, a crowd's field from the rule), the nuclear bindings (7a and 7b, a binding energy from the rule), the decays and the neutrino (8a to 8c, a lifetime and a mass ratio from the rule), the two arms in motion (5b, kept as the prediction page of the light-bound arms), complementarity and aberration (R5 and R6, their declarations), Bohr's ladder (6, replaced by the atom's lines), the bending (13, replaced by the delay under the hypothesis) and the period ratio (14, replaced by the fall under the hypothesis). No row is removed from the register; a row not predicted says so.









\paragraph{The prediction rows.} The (P) rows of Table~\ref{tab:list} are the algebra's own numbers with no known formula behind them: the atom's lines at the coupled modes, the index in motion, the moving block's clock on the two $64^3$ worlds, the ring-ups of the light clock, the two-pace bound, light's anisotropic dispersion on the sky and the bound clock's second term; each has its falsifier written before any run \cite[8.9]{algebra}, and a prediction is not a pass. The rows read on the engine before 2026-09-23, with their agreements and their disagreements, are history \cite{records}; what this version claims is the algebra's numbers before the runs, and the blanks of the table say so.



\subsection{Discussion and conclusions}\label{sec:discussion}

The chain from the click to Lorentz's factors, Einstein's step and Newton's form is Section~\ref{sec:click}; the two roads and their check are Section~\ref{sec:route}; what is proved opens Section~\ref{sec:physics}.





\paragraph{What the law names and has not computed.} Each item below is a computation the law's rules define, on a declared world with a declared click, that this paper has not made: the register holds no reading for it, nothing is claimed for it, and its verdict is NOT YET, NOT COMPARED or absent until a run is made and read by kind. (i) The lines of the atom: not a run not yet made but a rule the law lacks, no rule of the six quantising a body's loop and one click reaching only the loops with $2i^2 \ge j^2$ (the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 6; \cite{atomalgebra}); Bohr's $27/20$ waits on that rule, under its own identity; the ladder itself, $a_j/a_i = (j/i)^2$ and $E_j \propto 1/j^2$ with $27/20$, is conjectured from the algebra, not computed (item (viii) of the list above). (ii) Third-order interference, Sorkin's $\kappa_{\mathrm S}$ on a three-opening world (row 2c; no such world is registered). (iii) The single opening's spread against its pin (row 10), and the rows pinned without their run (4a, 5b, 11). (iv) The quarks and the nucleon: the quark families are in the catalog with their rational charges and their content per record (the families table \cite{records}, \texttt{u}), and no detector reading of a quarks world is registered; the nucleon as three measured events bound by the strong column, its read mass against the sum of its parts, is the reading that would test them \cite[record 248]{log}; colour, a $\Z_3$ label that passes the three tests and does nothing beside a colour force between rows that fails the vector and the local test, is designed under its own identity and not built \cite[record 270]{log}. (v) The unseen content: on the law's own rules the field at a galaxy's edge is Newton's in the shell mean and the detector adds nothing there; the one route to a flat rotation curve without unseen content, a short periodic dimension (\cite{hypotheses}, entry 6), fails nature's Tully-Fisher slope on a host map (\cite{darksector}, no run); what the law admits is unseen content as an input family, as nature's model does; no rotation curve is read after a detector and no disc under a declared unseen family is run. (vi) The size of the crowd's stretch, $g_1 = 0.36$, that the supernova diagram needs, from a declared content over a flight (an input in the dark energy item of the list above; the crowd's own accumulation gives the wrong sign), and the periodic GameBoard against the open one on the measured numbers, declared and not decided \cite[record 270]{log}. (vii) The detector's constants $c_j$ of the click's harmonics, not reached by the algebra (Section~\ref{sec:measurement}). (viii) The inverse square in space, pending its run (row 14); the bending's full deflection, its coefficient $2(1 + \gamma)$ on the one constant conjectured from the algebra; the ring's rule read inside its pins and the constant $4$ not closing within the grain (row 13). Apart from these stand the numbers for which the law has no formula and this paper offers none: the hierarchy $\rho_p$, the constant $h = h_q\Nphi$, the families' content per unit and the grain $\Nphi$, inputs by the dictionary (the forcing ledger \cite{records}). \paragraph{Positioning.} The click's assignment of the second outcome from the joint weights is a non-local step on the labels, its interval the last arm's (as after Theorem~\ref{th:marginals}), forced by Bell's theorem because the marginals are exact and $S > 2$
\cite{bell1964,chsh1969}; no-signalling of the counts is Theorem~\ref{th:marginals} \cite{grw1980}, and the order of the outcomes signals under the sequential wheel (Section~\ref{sec:bell}; the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 1c, FAIL BY DERIVATION, the order channel computed before any run \cite{orderderivation}). The click's
finite kinematics is Weyl's and Schwinger's on $\Z_{\Nphi}$
\cite{weyl1931,schwinger1960}; the transport a lattice gas's exact integer dynamics \cite{hpp1976,fhp1986}, the flight table's transport free of dispersion where the lattice automata of
\cite{bialynicki1994,meyer1996,arrighi2019} disperse, the record kind's not, its $k^2$ dispersion the prediction of row A2; the uniform $u$ does the work of quantum equilibrium \cite{bohm1952,dgz1992}; the model is $\psi$-ontic \cite{spekkens2007,hs2010}; Theorem~\ref{th:bell} puts $S(\Nphi)$ on
both sides of Tsirelson's bound \cite{tsirelson1980,pr1994}. The earlier testbed \cite{paper1} is history.

\section{Technical details}\label{app:technical}

\paragraph{The tables and their rounding.} The circle is $\Z_{\Nphi}$ with $4 \mid \Nphi$. The tables are
$C_{\Nphi}[p] = \mathrm{round}(256\cos(2\pi p/\Nphi))$ and $S_{\Nphi}[p] = C_{\Nphi}[p - \Nphi/4]$,
so $C_{\Nphi}[p + \Nphi/2] = -C_{\Nphi}[p]$ and $S_{\Nphi}[p + \Nphi/4] = C_{\Nphi}[p]$ exactly; the norm
$C_{\Nphi}^2 + S_{\Nphi}^2$ lies in $[65536 - 351,\ 65536 + 361]$ for every power of
two $\Nphi \le 65536$  \cite{checks}.   The normalisation by $C_K$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:rung} makes the click's probabilities sum to one at completion, and the paper claims exact unitarity nowhere.

\paragraph{The symbols.} The symbol table, every letter with its kind and its name, is in the paper's records file \cite{records}; every symbol is named at its first use in the text.



\section{Reproduction}\label{app:reproduction}

Every registered run's world file, its expectation written before the run, its source fingerprint and its record, the check scripts with their outputs, the figures' runs and the seven confirmations (each a run's clicks against the formula shown Inside, with its numbers) are listed in the paper's records file \cite{records} and in the registers \cite{register,replications}; the code and the worlds are the archive \cite{zenodo}. The archived version cited at submission is the tag \texttt{paper-2026-09-22} on the merge commit of the pull request that carries this cut, one tree whose history holds the trees named above and the log records this paper cites; it replaces the concept DOI below. The software, the computations, the derivations' checks and the text were made with a large language model as a tool under the author's direction and instructions, as the declaration at the end of the paper states; every decision is the author's. Every theorem, identity and number of the paper was re-derived and recomputed independently, one line per statement \cite{mathread}. The paper's law is the massive record kind with the local detector law, on \texttt{main} at a867ab22 \cite{algebra}; the beam law's runtime before the generic entry of the bending (the runs' own commits named above, on the first-parent line of \texttt{main} up to 3a9a7109, the last commit before the entry's merge 5b855791) is history, its flight table and its readings in the records file \cite{records}; the generic entry is a later rule of that runtime (Section~\ref{sec:law}, P9), and the ring's run (the full record \cite{nature,records}, row 13) is this paper's one reading under it. Every record, note, design and register row this text cites is on the tree of this cut (main merged into it at \texttt{87c7ec6b}).

The long form of this manuscript, with the derivation record of every formula, is the tree's paper at the commit \texttt{c15c1174}; the forty-page cut before it at \texttt{b0d1ebf7}.
